items.description: 🐧 Unified and Stable RSI Platform
items.readme_text:
PenguinHarness

Unified and Stable RSI Framework
Fully automatic optimization: any model · any algorithm · any benchmark

English | 简体中文

## Why PenguinHarness PenguinHarness is an open-source framework for agent self-evolution (recursive self-improvement, RSI). The model stays fixed; the harness evolves: prompts, Skills, tools and hooks. It runs on your computer or server as a desktop app, a Web App, a CLI and an SDK. - **Every RSI algorithm in one framework.** Default, OPRO, APE, ACE, AWM, SkillAdam, SkillOpt, OpenSkill and TRACE ship as plugins and run on the same built-in Benchmarks, scoreboard and snapshots. - **One sentence builds an agent app.** Describe what you need, and an agent writes the app, its page and its run instructions. - **Cheap to run.** A deliberately small toolset, tuned for open models: on our data-analysis suite, the best accuracy at 1/70 of Claude Code's cost. ## Self-evolution Pick an algorithm, pick a Benchmark, and an agent improves another agent round by round. Every candidate is a new version, snapshotted before it changes, and every score lands in the Evaluation Center. | Toolkit | Algorithm | | --- | --- | | `default-rsi-toolkit` | Trial, reflect, improve: one hypothesis and one change per round | | `opro-rsi-toolkit` | [OPRO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03409): new instructions from the history of scored ones | | `ape-rsi-toolkit` | [APE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.01910): candidate instructions induced from examples | | `ace-rsi-toolkit` | [ACE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618): lessons from Traces curated into a playbook | | `awm-rsi-toolkit` | [AWM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07429): workflows induced from successful runs | | `skilladam-rsi-toolkit` | [SkillAdam](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08944): evolving issue tracker and adaptive Skill edit budget | | `skillopt-rsi-toolkit` | [SkillOpt](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904): bounded Skill edits, score-based selection and cross-epoch reflection | | `openskill-rsi-toolkit` | [OpenSkill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06741): external research and independent virtual tests before frozen-State evaluation | | `trace-rsi-toolkit` | [TRACE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22793): skill-bank evolution from contrasting trajectories, with consistency measurement | | `rrsi-rsi-toolkit` | [RRSI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24972): annealed edit budget, a leakage Critic before any measurement, a Pruner for what stopped earning, and a noise-floored selection rule | Every new Project includes seventeen Benchmarks, run as Harbor tasks in Docker: PenguinHarness Benchmark Sec A to Sec E (from rag-bench-essential, DeepSWE, AutomationBench, Terminal-Bench-Science and Terminal-Bench) and a Train/Test pair for each of GDPEVO Essential's six scenarios. More are in [penguin-harness-benchmark](https://github.com/Prism-Shadow/penguin-harness-benchmark).

**Demo:** a decision agent is evaluated, revises its working method once, and is retested on the same model. Its score goes from 84 to 100, and the cost of every run is on screen. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7925b4b5-db78-4e00-b209-89deca394e34 ## One sentence, one app ```text Build a legal review agent with a simple workspace where users upload contracts, track the review, and download a report with risky clauses, explanations, and suggested revisions. ``` The result: a legal review app. Users upload contracts, follow each file's review, and download a report of risky clauses with explanations and suggested revisions. Five sample reviews cost $0.0423 in model calls. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28c0ef95-1dfa-47be-bad0-7326ccdf4e7c ## What agents can do
Browser automation
Agents drive your own Chrome through the PenguinHarness Browser extension, or the desktop app's built-in browser. They read pages as text and act through short scripts, so a step costs few tokens. Tutorial

 Workbenches
Every agent can have its own hot-reloaded workbench: ask for one and the agent writes the page and its server code. The workbench appears as a tab beside the agent's chat. Tutorial
Remote machines
Add a machine the server reaches over ssh. Conversations in a Workspace on that machine run on it, in the same window. Tutorial

 Agent API
One unified API connects any agent to any external app: send input over HTTP and read the run back as a stream of AMSP events. Tutorial
Replies can also carry UI: choices, forms, steps, Mermaid diagrams and live widgets ([A2UI](https://penguin.ooo/blog/penguinharness-0-2-15)). ## Results Each harness on the model it is usually paired with, on the same tasks:

## Built-in plugins Agents can also write and optimize their own Skills ([docs](https://penguin.ooo/docs/skills)). | Category | Plugins | | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Agent Self-Evolution | `default-rsi-toolkit`, `opro-rsi-toolkit`, `ape-rsi-toolkit`, `ace-rsi-toolkit`, `awm-rsi-toolkit`, `skilladam-rsi-toolkit`, `skillopt-rsi-toolkit`, `openskill-rsi-toolkit`, `trace-rsi-toolkit`, `rrsi-rsi-toolkit` | | Office Productivity | `a2ui`, `data-analysis`, `use-firecrawl`, `browser-automation`, `use-bento-slides`, `humanizer`, `goal`, `continual-learning`, `trace-lookup`, `agent-company`, `penguin-support` | | Software Development | `software-development`, `use-claude-code` | | AI App Development | `agent-development`, `agent-evaluation`, `model-development`, `skill-porting` | ## Supported models These are the model families we focus on supporting. The app's **Models** page lists each variant and its providers. ### Closed-source models | Model | Providers | | --- | --- | | GPT 6.1 | OpenAI, OpenRouter | | Claude 5.5 | Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go | | Gemini 4 | Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Penguin Go, OpenCode Go | | Grok 4.7 | OpenRouter, OpenCode Go | | Qwen3.8 Max | Qwen Token Plan, Qwen Pay-As-You-Go, OpenRouter, TokenDance, OpenCode Go | ### Open-source models | Model | Providers | | --- | --- | | DeepSeek V4.1 | DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, Atlas Cloud, TokenDance, Penguin Go, OpenCode Go, Qwen Token Plan, Qwen Pay-As-You-Go, ModelScope | | Kimi K3 | Moonshot AI, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, TokenDance, OpenCode Go, Qwen Pay-As-You-Go | | GLM 5.3 | Z.AI, OpenRouter, TokenDance, OpenCode Go | | Hunyuan 4 | OpenRouter, TokenDance, OpenCode Go | | MiMo v2.6 | OpenRouter, TokenDance, OpenCode Go | OpenCode Go offers Claude Haiku 5.5; Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 are available through Anthropic and OpenRouter. Hunyuan 4 uses `hy4-preview`. Custom OpenAI-protocol endpoints also work, covering 1000+ online and local models. ## Install ### Desktop app Download the installer from [penguin.ooo/download](https://penguin.ooo/download): macOS 11+ (dmg), Windows 10+ (exe) or Linux x64 (AppImage, deb). The app opens signed in and needs no terminal. ### CLI and server | Platform | Install command | | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `curl -fsSL https://penguin.ooo/install.sh \| sh` | | Windows (PowerShell) | `irm https://penguin.ooo/install.ps1 \| iex` | | npm (Node >= 24) | `npm install -g @prismshadow/penguin-cli` | Then run `penguin web`. It serves the Web App at `http://127.0.0.1:7364` and prints a first-login link until a password is set; models are configured on the **Models** page. The desktop app and the CLI share `~/.penguin/data`. ### Docker ```bash docker run -d --name penguin -p 127.0.0.1:7364:7364 -v penguin-data:/data hiyouga/penguinharness:0.2.18 docker logs penguin # the first-login link, openable as it stands on this machine ``` The image serves on port 7364 with its data on the `/data` volume, for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`; `latest` follows changes to the image's runtime or build inputs on `main`, and each release is also tagged with its version. The example listens on loopback only. For a network-facing deployment, Compose and upgrades, see the [Docker quickstart](https://penguin.ooo/docs/quickstart-docker).
Offline install (air-gapped machines) Every GitHub Release attaches exactly one package per target — Linux and macOS in x64 / arm64, Windows in x64, plus a runtime-less universal package. The same file serves online and offline installation. Each package seals the program payload, its SHA256 checksum and the platform's installer. Download the one file on a networked machine, copy it to the target, extract once and run the bundled installer — no network, no separate checksum file to carry (the sealed SHA256 is always verified). **Linux (on arm64, use `penguin-linux-arm64.tar.gz`):** ```bash mkdir penguin-install tar -xzf penguin-linux-x64.tar.gz -C penguin-install ./penguin-install/install.sh ``` **macOS (Apple silicon shown; on Intel, use `penguin-darwin-x64.tar.gz`):** ```bash mkdir penguin-install tar -xzf penguin-darwin-arm64.tar.gz -C penguin-install ./penguin-install/install.sh ``` **Windows (unzip, then double-click `install.cmd` — or run it in PowerShell):** ```powershell Expand-Archive penguin-win32-x64.zip -DestinationPath penguin-install cd penguin-install .\install.cmd ```
### Chrome extension (optional) [PenguinHarness Browser](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/penguinharness-browser/dodgfhpcbmkjfcbgnoidablfgjjhhmgp) lets agents drive the tabs you hand them in your own Chrome. ## CLI and SDK The same engine, scriptable, and made to be driven by agents: ```bash penguin config model add --provider deepseek --model-id deepseek-flash --api-key sk-... --set-default penguin run -m "Create hello.txt containing Hello, Penguin" # one-shot task penguin chat # interactive REPL (/compact, /clear, /exit, Ctrl-C to interrupt) penguin server # headless service (same API the Web App uses) ``` ```ts import { createAgent, isCompleteModelMessage, userText } from "@prismshadow/penguin-core"; const agent = await createAgent({ agentId: "default_agent" }); const session = await agent.createSession({ workspaceDir: process.cwd() }); for await (const output of session.run([userText("Create hello.txt containing hi")], { approve: async () => "allow", // per-tool-call approval })) { if (isCompleteModelMessage(output) && output.payload.type === "text") { console.log(output.payload.text); } } ``` ## Roadmap - [x] Public release of the benchmark suite - [x] Desktop app - [x] Windows support - [x] Agent company and templates - [ ] Company-level self-evolution - [ ] OpenShell integration (permission-governed shell) - More to come… ## Development ```bash pnpm install && pnpm build # build first: core's exports point at dist/ pnpm dev # backend + web app together (prefixed logs, deps built once) ``` Working on this repository with a coding agent: its development Skills are in `.agents/skills/` (`penguin-harness-dev`, `penguin-harness-frontend`, `penguin-harness-manual-test`, `penguin-harness-writing`). Claude Code loads them with no install, through the `.claude` → `.agents` symlink; for another agent, link or copy `.agents/skills/*` into the directory it reads Skills from. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full workspace guide: dev commands, quality gates, repo layout, and the changelog rule. ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who has contributed to PenguinHarness!

## Citation If you use PenguinHarness in your research, please cite: ```bibtex @software{penguinharness2026, author = {{PrismShadow Team}}, title = {PenguinHarness: Efficient Self-Improving Harness for Everyone}, year = {2026}, url = {https://github.com/Prism-Shadow/penguin-harness}, license = {Apache-2.0} } ``` ## Acknowledgements This repo benefits from: - [MinGit](https://github.com/git-for-windows/git): the POSIX shell and Git bundled on Windows - [GenericAgent](https://github.com/lsdefine/genericagent): built-in browser automation See [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) for their licenses. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) © 2026 Prism Shadow ## Maintenance team **Organizations:** PrismShadow AI, Qinghe Dynamic **Maintainers:** - Yaowei Zheng (LlamaFactory, PrismShadow) - Yangxi Xiang - Junhao Hu - Leijun Zhou (PrismShadow) - Zhihao Liu (PrismShadow) - Xiang Qu (PrismShadow) - Hengjin Dou (PrismShadow) - Ning Wang (Qinghe Dynamic) - Ming Lu (Qinghe Dynamic) Built with ❤️

items.name: AngelSlim
items.description: Model compression toolkit engineered for enhanced usability, comprehensiveness, and efficiency.
items.readme_text:
English | [简体中文](README_cn.md)

A more accessible, comprehensive, and efficient toolkit for large model compression.

✒️ TechnicalReport | 📖 Documentation | 🤗 Hugging Face | 🤖 ModelScope

💬 WeChat | 🫨 Discord

## 📣Latest News - [26/11/20] We've released FP8 quantized weights for **Hy4** ([Hy4-FP8](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-FP8)), along with FP8 and MXFP4 quantization toolkits and low-bit on-device GGUF models ([Hy4-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Hy4-GGUF)). 🔥🔥🔥 - [26/11/18] We've released FP8 quantized weights for **Hy4-flash** ([Hy4-flash-FP8](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-flash-FP8)), along with the quantization toolkit and low-bit on-device GGUF models ([Hy4-flash-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Hy4-flash-GGUF)). 🔥🔥🔥 - [26/10/26] We've released the Q4_K_M and Q8_0 quantized model for [Hy-SimulMT](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-SimulMT) on llama.cpp, supporting both the [translation-only model](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B-GGUF/tree/main) and [source text and translation](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B-Interleave-GGUF/tree/main)). ## 🛎️How to Use ### 1. Install AngelSlim We recommend using `pip` to install the latest stable version of `AngelSlim`: ```shell pip install angelslim ``` Alternatively, you can clone the repository and install from source in editable mode: ```shell cd AngelSlim && python setup.py install ``` > **Note:** AngelSlim integrates the speculative-decoding training framework [AngelSpec](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec) as a git submodule (under `third_party/AngelSpec/`). Clone with `--recursive`, or initialize in an existing clone: > > ```shell > # Clone with submodules > git clone --recursive https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSlim.git > # Or, in an already-cloned repo > git submodule update --init --recursive > ``` For more detailed installation instructions and platform-specific guidance, please refer to the [Installation Documentation](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/getting_started/installation.html). ### 2. Quick Start #### 2.1 Speculative Decoding AngelSlim's speculative-decoding training is powered by **[AngelSpec](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec)** (git submodule under `third_party/AngelSpec/`) — a torch-native framework for **training** speculative-decoding draft models, featuring a rich set of draft architectures, target-model support, and production-scale training. It supports a variety of draft methods, led by **DFly** and **MTP + TTT**. It follows a **disaggregated design**: inference engines run the frozen target model and extract multi-layer hidden states, which a [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake) store streams over RDMA (no disk staging) to the FSDP2 training workers, while a controller handles batching, backpressure, and evaluation. Inference and training run on separate GPU pools and scale independently. **Capabilities:** - **Multi-backend inference** — vLLM (first-class), SGLang, and HuggingFace. - **Long-sequence training** — Ulysses sequence parallelism (USP) for 128k+ contexts. - **Document-aware sequence packing** — with cross-document attention isolation. - **Online evaluation** — spec-decode acceptance rate measured during training. - **Multi-node** — large MoE target models sharded across nodes over Mooncake RDMA. - **Vocabulary pruning** — shrink the draft `lm_head` to a smaller token set at train or convert time. ```shell # Initialize the submodule (see Install section above) git submodule update --init --recursive cd third_party/AngelSpec # Install AngelSpec + the vLLM backend pip install -e ".[vllm]" # Hidden-state transport (not pulled in by the extras; install separately) pip install mooncake-transfer-engine # Single-node quickstart (4 GPUs: 2 inference + 2 training) ./examples/qwen3-8b-single-node/run.sh ``` For more details, see the [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25852), [AngelSpec docs](https://angelspec.readthedocs.io/), [AngelSpec README](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec/blob/main/README.md), and [Hugging Face weights](https://huggingface.co/collections/AngelSlim/angelspec). #### 2.2 LLM/VLM/Audio Model Quantization After installing `AngelSlim`, you can launch static FP8 quantization for the Qwen3-1.7B model with the following one-command script: ```shell python3 tools/run.py -c configs/qwen3/fp8_static/qwen3-1_7b_fp8_static.yaml ``` This example produces quantized model weights by performing PTQ calibration on a model loaded from HuggingFace. For **Hy3-preview** (MoE A20B) FP8-Static quantization: ```shell python tools/run.py -c configs/hunyuan/fp8_static/hunyuanv3_a20b_fp8_static_c8.yaml ```
Code-based Start To perform dynamic `FP8` quantization on `Qwen3-1.7B`: ```python from angelslim.engine import Engine slim_engine = Engine() # Prepare model slim_engine.prepare_model(model_name="Qwen", model_path="Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B",) # Initialize compressor slim_engine.prepare_compressor("PTQ", default_method="fp8_dynamic") # Compress model slim_engine.run() # Save compressed model slim_engine.save("./output") ```
For more details, please refer to the [Quick Start Documentation](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/getting_started/quickstrat.html). #### 2.3 Diffusion Model Quantization Use the `scripts/diffusion/run_diffusion.py` for quantization and inference: ```shell # Online quantization and inference python scripts/diffusion/run_diffusion.py \ --model-name-or-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell \ --quant-type fp8-per-tensor \ --prompt "A cat holding a sign that says hello world" \ --height 1024 --width 1024 --steps 4 --guidance 0.0 --seed 0 ``` For more quantization inference methods, please refer to [the Diffusion Model Quantization Documentation](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/features/diffusion/quantization.html). #### 2.4 Token Compression (VLM) AngelSlim provides a universal metadata-driven framework for vision token pruning and merging. You can quickly verify a compression strategy (e.g., **VisionZip**) with a smoke test: ```shell python tools/test_universal_pruning.py \ --model_path "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct" \ --config "configs/qwen2_5_vl/pruning/visionzip_r0.9.yaml" ``` For more details on implementing new strategies, please refer to the [Token Compressor Documentation](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/features/token_compressor/index.html). ### 3. Deployment and Testing #### 3.1 Offline Inference To test offline inference with a quantized model loaded via `transformers`.
Run script details ```shell python scripts/deploy/offline.py $MODEL_PATH "Hello, my name is" ``` Where `MODEL_PATH` is the path to the quantized model output.
#### 3.2 API Service Deployment After specifying the quantized model path `MODEL_PATH`, you can deploy an OpenAI-compatible API service using **vLLM** and **SGLang** inference frameworks.
Run script details - **vLLM** Use the following script to launch a [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) server, recommended version `vllm>=0.8.5.post1`. For MOE INT8 quantized models, vllm>=0.9.0 is required. ```shell bash scripts/deploy/run_vllm.sh --model-path $MODEL_PATH --port 8080 -d 0,1,2,3 -t 4 -p 1 -g 0.8 --max-model-len 4096 ``` Where `-d` is the visible devices, `-t` is tensor parallel size, `-p` is pipeline parallel size, and `-g` is the GPU memory utilization. - **SGLang** Use the following script to launch a [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) server, recommended version `sglang>=0.4.6.post1`. ```shell bash scripts/deploy/run_sglang.sh --model-path $MODEL_PATH --port 8080 -d 0,1,2,3 -t 4 -g 0.8 ```
#### 3.3 Service Invocation Invoke requests via [OpenAI's API format](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/introduction).
Run script details ```shell bash scripts/deploy/openai.sh -m $MODEL_PATH -p "Hello, my name is" --port 8080 --max-tokens 4096 --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20 --repetition-penalty 1.05 --system-prompt "You are a helpful assistant." ``` where `-p` is the input prompt.
#### 3.4 Performance Evaluation Evaluate the performance of quantized model using [lm-evaluation-harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness), recommended version`lm-eval>=0.4.8`.
Run script details ```shell bash scripts/deploy/lm_eval.sh -d 0,1 -t 2 -g 0.8 -r $RESULT_PATH -b "auto" --tasks ceval-valid,mmlu,gsm8k,humaneval -n 0 $MODEL_PATH ``` where `RESULT_PATH` is the directory for saving test results, `-b` is batch size, `--tasks` specifies the evaluation tasks, and `-n` is the number of few-shot examples.
For more detaileds, please refer to the [Deployment Documentation](https://angelslim.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/deployment/deploy.html). ## 📈 Benchmark ### 1. #### 1.2 ⚡ D-cut — Breaking the Concurrency Ceiling When concurrency climbs, target verification becomes the bottleneck and rejected draft suffixes clog the batch. **D-cut** treats verification as a shared batch budget — ranking each request's verification depth by expected gain / cost, deepening drafts when the system is idle and trimming them when it's slammed. The payoff lands exactly where DFly plateaus: past concurrency 48, D-cut keeps turning load into throughput, up to **+15.7%** over DFly at near-zero quality cost (accepted length 2.50 → 2.46).

items.name: Lody
items.description: Share coding agents with your team on phone and desktop
items.readme_text:
Lody

English | 简体中文

A shared workspace for the coding agents your team already uses.

Connect any machine and bring any coding agent through ACP. Share conversations with your team and dispatch work from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI.

Documentation | Getting Started

## What you can do with Lody ### Share Agent conversations with your team Open the same conversation with your teammates. See the full transcript, runtime status, files, and code changes around the work, then add instructions without passing around screenshots or pasted logs. ### Bring the Agents and machines you already use Connect Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, OpenCode, or another ACP-compatible Agent. Keep using the subscriptions, logins, models, and permission modes configured on your laptops, workstations, servers, and cloud VMs. Machines remain private until their owner shares them with the workspace. ### Dispatch work from any surface Choose any connected machine when dispatching work from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI. Permission requests, progress, conversations, and code changes stay visible across these surfaces. ## Connect a machine Run Lody on a workstation, server, or cloud VM: ```bash npx lody daemon start ``` The command opens a sign-in link, connects the machine to your workspace, and keeps it available for work dispatched from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI. ## Use Lody from the CLI The CLI is more than the process that connects a machine. From a terminal or script, you can register local projects; inspect workspaces, machines, linked repositories, and Agent configs; create and message sessions; read their history and status; or archive and restore them. Commands that support `--json` can also feed Lody workspace data into your own tools. ```bash npx lody session create --workspace my-team --agent-config codex \ --repo owner/repo "Fix the failing test" npx lody session list --workspace my-team ``` See the [CLI documentation](https://lody.ai/docs/cli) for the full command reference. ## Let Agents coordinate work across conversations Lody gives Agents tools to create or reuse other conversations, read their status and history, send follow-up instructions, cancel running work, and bring results back. This lets one conversation act as the coordinator: you can analyze a bug with a main Agent, then have it delegate investigation, implementation, and testing to separate conversations running in parallel. Lody keeps each child conversation independent while preserving its relationship to the conversation that created it. Conversations can also be referenced with an `@` mention when you or an Agent needs to connect work across sessions. ## Keep code and execution in the same workspace ### Keep parallel work isolated Give sessions their own Git worktrees so Agents can work in parallel without mixing changes. Open multiple chats, files, diffs, terminals, and previews in tabs, or fork a session into another conversation or worktree to explore a different approach. ### Inspect changes where the work happened Browse project files and inspect per-turn or full-session diffs beside the conversation. Add line-level comments, follow pull request status and CI, and keep GitHub review threads close to the Agent that produced the change.

### Give Agents visual feedback Open a running web app inside the session, switch between responsive viewports, and send element-level visual annotations back to the Agent.

## More built in - **Agent Roles** — share reusable Agent, model, permission, and instruction presets with the team. - **Attachments** — send files and images from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI, and receive files produced by Agents. - **Session tools** — search, pin, archive, fork, and organize conversations without losing their history. - **Desktop tools** — use a built-in terminal, command palette, customizable shortcuts, and open files in your editor. - **Mobile controls** — receive notifications, approve permission requests, inspect diffs, and follow active work with iOS Live Activities. - **Usage visibility** — see context, token and quota usage, plus machine and Agent resource consumption.

## Beyond conversations Shared conversations are Lody's starting point, not the whole workspace. We plan to add documents and document sandboxes so teams can shape requirements, preserve decisions, and work with Agents outside the timeline of a single conversation. Over time, these tools can become shared team context for understanding not only what changed, but why. We want the entire workspace—not only conversations—to become local-first. Lody uses the [Loro](https://loro.dev/) Stack, including Loro and Flock, to represent and synchronize collaborative state with CRDTs. The same foundation can extend from conversations to documents and future workspace tools. Our goal is for team context to become more durable and portable, and ultimately remain under the team's control. Lody is still moving toward full local-first support. ## Releases Pushing a stable `vX.Y.Z` tag creates a draft PR synchronizing every `apps/*/package.json` version on the default branch, followed by a GitHub Release with generated changelog notes. No installers or auto-update files are built or uploaded. The original tag is not moved; version synchronization takes effect on the default branch after the PR is merged. GitHub Actions must be allowed to create pull requests in repository settings. Bot-created PRs may require a maintainer action to trigger CI. Existing releases and their assets are preserved on reruns. ## Repository - `apps/cli` — Connect machines and run coding agents - `apps/electron` — Lody desktop app - [`apps/mobile`](apps/mobile/README.md) — New native iOS and Android clients - `packages/components` — Shared workspace UI - `packages/ui` — Base UI primitives and StyleX design tokens - `packages/platform` — Platform capabilities and integrations - `packages/shared` — Shared schemas, protocols, and utilities - `packages/cloud-api` — Optional-cloud protocol names and DTOs - `packages/e2ee-core` — End-to-end encryption library: signed ledger, key delivery, services and adapters ([reading guide](packages/e2ee-core/README.md)). Product hosts: [workspace bootstrap](.agents/docs/e2ee-workspace-bootstrap.md) - `packages/e2ee-client` — Personal-device E2EE host - `packages/e2ee-machine-sharing` — Machine-service sharing policy - `packages/e2ee-lab` — Local adversarial consumers and persistence probes for `@lody/e2ee-core` - `packages/turn-diff-store` — Local content-addressed turn snapshots - `packages/loro-streams-rpc` — RPC over Loro Streams - `packages/iroh-native` — Native iroh transport for encrypted-workspace RPC ([rules](packages/iroh-native/AGENTS.md)) - `packages/acp-extension-{core,kimi,pi}` — ACP extension submodule workspaces. Kimi and Pi stay outside the root pnpm graph - `site-docs` — Website, documentation, and blog - [`skills`](skills/lody-cli/SKILL.md) — Agent skills for Lody users, such as `lody-cli` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and the community PR size policy. ## Mobile and upstream credit Lody’s new native mobile clients live in [apps/mobile](apps/mobile/README.md). They are under active development and keep independent iOS and Android build toolchains; see the mobile README for setup and current scope. The iOS client is built directly on **[Innei’s lody-ios](https://github.com/Innei/lody-ios)**. We thank [Innei](https://github.com/Innei) and the upstream contributors for the native app, chat experience, application architecture, and Loro/Flock protocol runtime that made this work possible. Android also reuses a provenance-tracked snapshot of that runtime. This is substantial foundational work, not merely inspiration. Upstream licenses, notices, and additional acknowledgements are preserved in the [mobile credits](apps/mobile/README.md#credits-and-origins).

on GitHub](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd)** — it's free, made by one developer, and stars are how other people find it. ![SoloMD editor](web/public/demo/solomd-demo.svg) > ### 🤖 Built and maintained by Claude > > SoloMD is written, tested and released almost entirely by **Claude Code**, Anthropic's > coding agent, working under a human maintainer who sets the direction and decides what > ships. **Issues and pull requests are triaged and answered by Claude as well** — the > replies you get here are written by an AI, not typed by a person. > > We are telling you this for two reasons. You should know what you are trusting with your > notes: read the code, it is MIT and all of it is public. And when a reply is confidently > wrong — it happens — say so in the thread. That correction is the mechanism. > > **💼 For Teams & Founders (100% Async Contracts):** Using this exact human-architect + Claude Code pipeline, the maintainer also built **[Unterm](https://unterm.app)** — a self-developed Rust + wgpu terminal kernel exposing 152 MCP methods with an Action Gateway. Available for **100% asynchronous remote contracts** (custom MCP servers, Rust/Tauri agentic desktop apps, and AI workflows — written specs, Loom demos & clean PRs, zero meetings). [**Work with the architect →**](https://doaipm.com/en/about/?utm_source=solomd_readme#work-with-me) Your notes live in a plain folder. **SoloMD gives you Typora’s quiet, centered writing feel, Obsidian’s local-first vault links, free encrypted sync across all 5 platforms, built-in 9-format export, and zero-config local AI + a 16-tool MCP server.** Built on Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + CodeMirror 6 + Rust. ~14 MB on Windows, ~16 MB on Linux (`.deb`/`.rpm`), ~21 MB on Android (`arm64`), and ~30 MB for the dual-arch macOS Universal `.dmg`. Free, MIT-licensed, no account, no subscription, no plugin tax, no SoloMD-hosted servers. Your notes, AI keys, embeddings index, and git history stay on your device. ## What's new in v5.0 – v5.2 - **Three seamless writing modes (`v5.2`)** — Switch anytime between **Pure WYSIWYG** (Markdown syntax markers stay completely hidden even on the active caret line), **Live Preview** (markers reveal only on the active line), and synced **Split / Source** view. - **Unified 9-Format Export Center (`v5.2`)** — One modal with live preview exports **PDF** (with KaTeX & Mermaid), **Word (`.docx`)**, **HTML**, **EPUB**, **LaTeX**, **ODT**, **RTF**, **Plain Text**, and **Markdown** out of the box — **zero external Pandoc installation required**. - **Zero-config local AI (OPR) + 20+ BYOK providers (`v5.2`)** — One-click Open Provider Registry (OPR) auto-discovery detects local **Ollama**, **LM Studio**, **Jan**, **vLLM**, and **llama.cpp** servers on localhost. Or plug in your own API key for 20+ cloud providers (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, Doubao, MiniMax, Groq, Mistral, xAI, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter, etc.) stored in your OS keychain. - **Vault-scoped encrypted Cloud & Git sync (`v5.2`)** — Bind each workspace independently to **iCloud Drive**, **OneDrive**, **Nutstore**, **Baidu/Aliyun Drive**, **Syncthing**, **WebDAV**, **S3 / Cloudflare R2**, or **GitHub / GitLab / Gitea** — with optional **AES-256-GCM / XChaCha20-Poly1305** end-to-end encryption and conflict copy protection. - **Lightweight declarative JSON extensions (`v5.2`)** — Drop simple JSON manifests into `/.solomd/plugins/*.json` (or manage via *Settings → Extensions*) to add custom `/` slash templates, regex/template Command Palette transforms, and one-click Webhook publishers — zero Electron plugin bloat. - **CLI v2 & 16-tool MCP server (`v5.2`)** — `solomd open / new / list / search / export / daily / agent / mcp` from your terminal, plus `solomd-mcp` with multi-vault `--workspace` federation. ## Three pillars in one lightweight native app 1. **Calm writing & publishing.** Pure WYSIWYG + Live Preview + Split view, floating selection formatting bar, Focus & Typewriter modes, fullscreen Slideshow (`⌘⌥P`), Vim mode, KaTeX math + Mermaid diagrams, image paste to `_assets/`, built-in 9-format export, and `.docx / .pdf / .xlsx / .pptx` drag-and-drop import to Markdown. First-class CJK encoding detection (UTF-8 / GBK / Big5 / Shift-JIS), character counts, and Simplified ↔ Traditional conversion. 2. **Connected local vault across 5 platforms.** Native apps for **macOS, Windows (x64 + ARM64), Linux (x64 + ARM64), iOS/iPadOS, and Android** with cross-device session restore. `[[Wikilinks]]`, backlinks, YAML frontmatter properties, 100% offline semantic RAG search (`⌘⇧F`), AutoGit snapshot on every `⌘S` (libgit2 built in), and free vault-scoped encrypted sync. 3. **Local AI & MCP endpoint.** Inline AI rewrite (`⌘J`), right-side Agent Panel (streamed chat-with-vault, `[[wikilink]]` citations, inline tool cards), OPR local model auto-discovery + 20+ BYOK providers, and the bundled `solomd-mcp` binary exposing 16 tools to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, and Claude Code. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | **3 Editing Modes** *(v5.2)* | **Pure WYSIWYG** (no syntax shift on active line), **Live Preview**, and synced **Split / Source** view. | | **Unified 9-Format Export** *(v5.2)* | Built-in live-preview export to PDF, DOCX, HTML, EPUB, LaTeX, ODT, RTF, TXT, and MD — no external Pandoc setup needed. | | **Vault-Scoped Cloud & Git Sync** *(v5.2)* | Per-workspace sync via iCloud, OneDrive, Nutstore, Baidu/Aliyun Drive, Syncthing, WebDAV, S3/R2, or GitHub/GitLab/Gitea with optional E2EE. | | **OPR Local AI + 20+ BYOK** *(v5.2)* | Auto-discover local Ollama / LM Studio / Jan / vLLM / llama.cpp, or use 20+ BYOK cloud providers. Keys live in your OS keychain. | | **Declarative JSON Extensions** *(v5.2)* | `.solomd/plugins/*.json` adds custom `/slash` templates, regex/template text transforms, and one-click Webhook publishing. | | **Agent Panel & AI Rewrite** | Streamed chat-with-vault (`[[wikilink]]` citations, Insert/Copy to note) and `⌘J` inline selection rewrite/translate. | | **Bundled 16-Tool MCP Server** | `solomd-mcp` ships in the app. Supports `--workspace path1 --workspace path2` multi-vault federation, stdio (default) and loopback Streamable HTTP. | | **AutoGit per note** | Every `⌘S` commits a snapshot to a local `.git` inside your workspace. libgit2 vendored, no system git required. Visual diff & 1-click rollback. | | **Offline Semantic Search (RAG)** | `⌘⇧F` ranks paragraphs by meaning across your vault using an on-device Rust embedder — zero model downloads, zero network calls. | ## Use it **1. Write, link, and export.** Open any folder of `.md` files. Switch between Pure WYSIWYG, Live Preview, and Split view in the top header; press `⌘⇧E` (or *File → Export*) to open the Unified 9-Format Export Center. **2. Chat with your vault or rewrite inline.** Select text and press `⌘J` for inline AI rewrite/translation, or open the right-side Agent Panel (`⌘⇧P` → *View: Toggle Agent Panel*) for multi-turn chat across your notes. Click **Auto-detect Local Models** in *Settings → AI* to connect local Ollama / LM Studio in one click. **3. Drive your vault from Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Claude Code:** ```bash # Print the MCP config snippet for your AI client… solomd mcp-config # …or register it automatically across AI clients on your machine: solomd mcp install ``` ```json { "mcpServers": { "solomd": { "command": "/Applications/SoloMD.app/Contents/MacOS/solomd-mcp", "args": ["--workspace", "/Users/me/Documents/SoloMD"] } } } ``` For multi-vault federation, repeat `--workspace`: ```json "args": [ "--workspace", "/Users/me/Documents/SoloMD", "--workspace", "/Users/me/Documents/work-notes" ] ``` **4. Or hand a prompt to `claude` / `codex` CLI directly:** ```bash solomd agent "summarize this week's daily notes into a weekly review and commit it" ``` ### MCP tools (16 built in) | Kind | Tools | |---|---| | Read (always on) | `list_notes`, `read_note`, `search`, `get_backlinks`, `get_outline`, `list_tags`, `list_tasks`, `autogit_log`, `autogit_diff`, `sync_status`, `share_url`, `read_agent_trace` | | Write (`--allow-write`) | `write_note`, `append_to_note`, `autogit_rollback`, `export_note` | Transports: stdio (default, what Claude Desktop / Cursor / Cline / Codex use), or Streamable HTTP for local/hosted clients: ```bash solomd-mcp --workspace ~/Documents/SoloMD --transport http --bind 127.0.0.1:8765 --auth-token "$TOKEN" ``` ### Command line (CLI v2) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhitongblog/solomd/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | bash solomd help ``` Commands: `open`, `new`, `daily`, `list`, `search`, `cat`, `export`, `agent`, `mcp list|install|uninstall|config`, `mcp-config`, `--version`. ## Install Latest release (**v5.2.0**) and every download: [**GitHub Releases**](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/latest) · [**AtomGit Mirror**](https://atomgit.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/tag/v5.2.0) · [**Gitee Mirror**](https://gitee.com/zhitong45/solomd/releases/tag/v5.2.0). **System requirements:** Windows 10+, macOS 10.15+, current mainstream Linux, iOS 15+, Android 7+ (API 24). ### macOS — universal dmg (Apple Silicon + Intel, signed + notarized) ```bash brew install --cask zhitongblog/solomd/solomd ``` Or one-line shell install: ```bash curl -fsSL https://solomd.app/install.sh | bash ``` Or direct download: [`SoloMD_5.2.0_universal.dmg`](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/download/v5.2.0/SoloMD_5.2.0_universal.dmg) · [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/solomd/id6762498874) ### Windows — x64 & ARM64 - [`SoloMD_5.2.0_x64_en-US.msi`](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/download/v5.2.0/SoloMD_5.2.0_x64_en-US.msi) / [`SoloMD_5.2.0_arm64_en-US.msi`](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/download/v5.2.0/SoloMD_5.2.0_arm64_en-US.msi) / portable `.zip` on [the releases page](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/latest) ```powershell irm https://solomd.app/install.ps1 | iex ``` ```powershell winget install solomd ``` ### Linux — x86_64 + aarch64 - `.AppImage` (universal), `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu), `.rpm` (Fedora/RHEL) — both architectures on [the releases page](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/latest). - Arch Linux: [`solomd-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/solomd-bin) on AUR. ### iOS / iPadOS & Android - **iPhone & iPad:** [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/solomd/id6762498874) - **Android:** [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.solomd) or direct [`SoloMD_5.2.0_universal.apk`](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/releases/download/v5.2.0/SoloMD_5.2.0_universal.apk) ## Compared | | SoloMD v5.2 | Obsidian | Typora | MarkText | |---|---|---|---|---| | License | **MIT (Open Source)** | Proprietary (free) | Paid ($14.99) | MIT (dormant since 2023) | | Stack | Tauri 2 (Rust + native WebView) | Electron | Electron | Electron | | Platforms | **macOS · Win · Linux · iOS · Android** | macOS · Win · Linux · iOS · Android | macOS · Win · Linux | macOS · Win · Linux | | Installer | **~14 MB (Win) / ~16 MB (Linux) / ~30 MB (Mac Universal)** | ~110 MB | ~70 MB | ~80 MB | | **Pure WYSIWYG + Live Preview + Split** | **✅ All 3 modes** | 🟡 Live Preview only | ✅ | ✅ | | **Built-in 9-format export (no Pandoc install)** | **✅ v5.2** | 🟡 PDF only (plugins for others) | 🟡 Requires external Pandoc | ❌ | | **Free vault-scoped cloud & Git sync** | **✅ iCloud / OneDrive / WebDAV / S3 / Git** | ❌ ($96/yr Obsidian Sync) | ❌ | ❌ | | **End-to-end encryption** | **✅ On your own storage** | ✅ Paid Obsidian Sync only | ❌ | ❌ | | **Zero-config local AI (OPR auto-detect)** | **✅ Ollama / LM Studio / Jan / vLLM** | 🟡 Community plugins | ❌ | ❌ | | **BYOK AI providers built in** | **✅ 20+ providers (OS keychain)** | 🟡 1–2 per community plugin | ❌ | ❌ | | **MCP server bundled** | **✅ 16 tools + multi-vault federation** | ❌ (community plugins) | ❌ | ❌ | | **Declarative JSON extensions** | **✅ `.solomd/plugins/*.json`** | ✅ Heavy JS plugins | ❌ | ❌ | | **Local semantic RAG search** | **✅ 100% offline in Rust** | 🟡 Community plugins | ❌ | ❌ | | **Version history per note** | **✅ AutoGit (libgit2 built in)** | 🟡 Manual git plugin | ❌ | ❌ | | **CJK encodings (GBK / Big5) + OpenCC** | **✅ Auto-detect** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Detailed breakdowns: [vs Obsidian](https://solomd.app/compare/vs-obsidian) · [vs Typora](https://solomd.app/compare/vs-typora) · [vs Tolaria](https://solomd.app/compare/vs-tolaria) · [vs MarkText](https://solomd.app/compare/vs-marktext). ## Privacy & security Pure client-side. Your `.md` files stay in the folder you chose. API keys live in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Linux libsecret), never in `localStorage` or any config file. AI requests go direct from your machine to the provider you picked — no SoloMD relay. RAG embeddings and the AutoGit repo are local-only. The MCP server speaks stdio by default; its optional HTTP transport binds to loopback unless you choose otherwise, and can require a bearer token. The whole codebase is MIT and auditable. E2EE sync uses AES-256-GCM (`.solomd-enc` cloud drive sync) and Argon2id → XChaCha20-Poly1305 (Git/remote sync). Plaintext stays on your devices; the remote sees only ciphertext. Path-traversal guards reject `..` segments and unauthorized paths across all Tauri and MCP endpoints. Full writeup: . ## Build from source Prereqs: Rust (stable), Node 18+, pnpm. ```bash git clone https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd.git cd solomd/app pnpm install pnpm tauri dev # dev with hot reload pnpm tauri build # release artifacts → src-tauri/target/release/bundle/ ``` Linux additionally needs `libdbus-1-dev` for the keychain backend. The MCP server is a separate crate at `mcp-server/`; the dev MCP harness used for end-to-end testing lives at `dev-mcp/`. End-to-end test entry point: `scripts/v4-self-test.sh` (run with `--with-release --with-ollama --with-ui` for full coverage). ## Contributing Issues and PRs welcome — [open one](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/issues). For a sense of direction, see [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md). The v4.0 build log is at [solomd.app/blog/v4-0-0-how-we-built-it/](https://solomd.app/blog/v4-0-0-how-we-built-it/) — start there if you want to understand the engineering principles before sending a PR. ## Contact / 联系 One maintainer, two front doors. Async on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/zhitongblog/solomd/discussions). Real-time chat: - **Telegram (international):** [@SOLOMDAPP](https://t.me/SOLOMDAPP) — release announcements + chat - **WeChat (中文):** scan to add me — note "SoloMD" 注明 SoloMD 直接通过 ## Sponsors Thank you to everyone who sponsors SoloMD: **tyysoft(太阳雨)** *(Note: This is a partial opt-in list — WeChat Pay, Alipay, and App Store / Google Play in-app tips are anonymous by default. If you supported SoloMD and would like your name listed, please open an issue or see [solomd.app/thanks](https://solomd.app/thanks).)* > **✨ 100% Free Forever & Supporter Badge:** Every feature in SoloMD is 100% free forever — no paywalls, no subscriptions, no ads. To support independent open-source development, you can sponsor via [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/zhitongblog) / [PayPal / Alipay / WeChat Pay](https://solomd.app/#sponsor), or use the 3 optional one-time in-app tip tiers on **Mac App Store, iOS App Store, and Google Play** (`☕ Buy a Coffee $0.99` · `🍜 Buy a Lunch $2.99` · `🚀 Generous Support $9.99`) to permanently unlock the exclusive **`✨ Supporter`** badge in Settings and About. ## Contributors Thank you to everyone who helps make SoloMD better — sponsors 💵, testers 🐛🤔, code/theme/packaging contributors 💻🎨📦 and promoters 📣 ([All Contributors](https://allcontributors.org) spec). Full wall of thanks: [solomd.app/thanks](https://solomd.app/thanks) · Promote SoloMD: [solomd.app/promote](https://solomd.app/promote)

items.name: poki
items.description: Poki uses your iPhone like you do. An open-source agent app that runs on your iPhone, reads the screen, and taps, types and swipes in real apps with your own model account.
items.readme_text:
Copy this prompt and send it to your coding agent

```text Install Poki on my iPhone from https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki ```

Connect your iPhone over USB and unlock it first. A free Apple Account works.

English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español
poki.bot

If Poki is useful to you, click ★ Star to support the project.

## What Poki is Poki is an open-source iPhone agent that operates your entire iPhone for you. The Poki app runs directly on your iPhone, reads the screen, and taps, types, and scrolls inside real apps using your own model account. You choose how it asks for permission; payments, deletions, and Wallet actions always stop for your confirmation.

## Why Poki

- **Skip multi-app tapping for everyday errands.** Ask Poki in chat, hold the Action Button, or trigger Siri to look things up in the built-in browser, check tomorrow's weather, or create a note. On iPhone Duo, Poki works across two apps side by side in Split View. - **Run saved skills by tap or by voice.** Launch a saved skill from the home screen instead of repeating the same steps every day, or start a hands-free spoken chat with Talk to Poki while Dynamic Island tracks each step. - **Automate your real phone without keeping a computer on.** Once installed from a Mac or Windows PC, Poki runs standalone on your iPhone with no computer attached and pauses on the Lock Screen or in Dynamic Island whenever a step needs approval. ## How to use ### Install Poki on your iPhone 1. **Install once from a Mac or Windows PC.** Connect and unlock your iPhone over USB (a free Apple Account works), then tell your coding agent, such as Claude Code or Codex: ```text Install Poki on my iPhone from https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki ``` Or download [Poki Setup](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki/releases) for macOS (`.dmg`) or Windows (`.exe`) and follow the window. 2. **Connect and add your model account.** Accept **Trust**, turn on Developer Mode and Automation Mode when iOS asks, set up an external connection routing `10.7.0.1` back to your iPhone (such as free LocalDevVPN), and sign in with ChatGPT Plus or Pro or paste an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go, or an OpenAI-compatible server). 3. **Run your first task.** Open Poki and send: ```text Create a new note in Notes titled "Poki Demo" with these three lines: Milk, Eggs, Coffee. Open the note when finished. Leave existing notes unchanged. ``` Open Notes afterward to confirm "Poki Demo" exists with those three lines.
Requirements, updating, common questions, and guides | | Requirement | | --- | --- | | iPhone | iOS 18 or later (iPhone XS, XR, SE 2nd gen or newer; iPadOS 18+ on iPad). Tested on physical iPhones with iOS 27. | | Computer | Mac with macOS 14+ (Node.js 24+ for agent install) or Windows PC (x64) with Apple Devices or iTunes. | | Cable and account | USB data cable and an Apple Account. Poki Setup renews free 7-day signatures while open, or sign in inside Poki. | | Connection | External connection routing `10.7.0.1` back to the iPhone (LocalDevVPN, Karing, or Shadowrocket). | | Model account | ChatGPT Plus/Pro sign-in, an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go), or an OpenAI-compatible server. | - Agent installer skill and Poki Setup: [install-poki skill](skills/install-poki/SKILL.md) and [Poki Setup](desktop/README.md) - Verification, limits, and release channels: [Verification](docs/verification.md) and [Release channels](docs/release-channels.md) - Earlier computer-driven tools (no longer updated): [Poki MCP and Poki Agent](docs/poki-mcp.md)
- Full installation, updating, FAQ, known issues, and roadmap: [Poki iPhone App Guide](docs/iphone-guide.md) - Changelog and version history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) ## Community - **Questions and ideas:** Join [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki/discussions). - **Bugs and requests:** Open an issue in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki/issues). - **Contribute code:** Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). See all contributors in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributors).
