items.readme_text:
简体中文 · English

# GraphAgent > 跑动态工作流的终端编码智能体：主智能体自己设计依赖图，子智能体按波次并行执行，状态持久化，崩溃后能恢复。 [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20Apache--2.0-blue)](#起源与许可) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/stargazers) GraphAgent 是独立的终端编码智能体，专注动态 DAG 工作流。它起源于 opencode 的早期版本，从 v2.0 起完全独立维护。 单个智能体循环处理一步到位的任务没有问题。任务一旦有先后依赖、有能并行的部分、中途还要过一道审查，它就吃力了：本该并行的活被串着跑，中间结论也没人复核。进程一挂，只能从头来。GraphAgent 让主智能体先把任务画成一张依赖图，再按图执行。图不是预先写死的，是它按任务现设计的，所以 DAG 工作流基本上就是动态工作流。 图里每个节点是一个真实的子会话，有自己的智能体和上下文窗口；依赖都满足的节点算一个波次，同一波次里并行跑。状态以事件持久化，所以能暂停、单步、重规划，崩溃后按持久化的记录恢复，不会凭空重放模型调用。 ## 项目状态 v2.0 开发中，即将发布。发布进度在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪；可复现的问题请提 [Issue](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues)。 ## 核心能力 | 能力 | 说明 | | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | DAG 工作流 | 主智能体设计依赖图，每个节点是真实的子会话，按波次并行；状态持久化，可暂停、恢复、重规划；节点超时从拿到执行槽位起算，排队时间不计 | | 统一子运行 | `task` 与 DAG 节点共用 ChildRun：每次委派一条持久记录，统一归属校验、取消和结果投递；子会话只接受主 agent 通信 | | 前后台委派 | 提示词准则决定 `task` 在前台等待还是后台运行；后台结果完成时以一条消息回注，不打断主会话 | | 只读 review | 内置只读 `review` agent；`/review` 默认后台执行，结论由主会话转述 | | 思考塑形 🧪 | 实验性功能，默认关闭 | | 项目记忆 | `/memory`，只保存你确认过的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用 | | Goal / Loop | `/goal`、`/subgoal`，外部 judge 判断进度，有回合预算 | | 定时提醒 | `/remind`，持久化的定时提醒；会话忙时等回合结束再送达，关闭期间到期的重启后补发 | | Hooks | 兼容 Claude Code hooks 协议 | | 上下文管理 | 工具输出限制、工具调用上限、长会话压缩 | ### DAG 工作流 主智能体觉得任务值得拆，就自己建图，不用你开口；你也可以用 `/dag-auto <任务>` 直接要求。边只表示“下游要读上游的产出”，没有这层关系的节点就并行。负责审查和仲裁的节点叫门禁，输出 ACCEPT、REVISE、REJECT 或 BLOCKED，下游可以按裁定决定跑不跑。TUI 里有 DAG 检查器，能看各波次和节点的实时状态，也能进入任何一个节点的子会话。 模型分层写在 `.agents/settings.json` 的 `dag.model`（判断、验收和评审节点用 advanced，写代码和探索这类跑量的用 standard），常用的图存进 `.agents/workflows/`，之后按名字就能启动。精选模板在 [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)。节点的 `timeout_ms` 从拿到执行槽位开始计时，排队时间不计。崩溃恢复只认持久化的记录。引擎不假设有跨进程的锁，也不保证节点恰好执行一次。用法和引擎细节见 [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)。 ### 子运行与通信 `task` 和 DAG 节点共用同一套 ChildRun。一次委派对应一条持久记录，记录归属、状态与结算结果；后台运行结束后结果只投递一次，重启或进程丢失的运行也会补投。子会话不接受自由输入：HTTP 操作层对子会话的写请求返回 409，只放行权限回复和只读旁问；引擎准入要求携带当前运行的 live 凭证。 `agent` 工具负责主会话与 DAG 节点之间的观察和消息：`observe` 分页查看节点进度与尝试，`send` 向确切的活跃尝试投递，`receive` 读取邮箱。节点需要澄清时问父会话，不直接问用户。工具只在存在活跃 DAG 节点运行时出现，可见性由进程内注册表判定，不查数据库。 ### 只读 review 与前后台分类 `/review` 使用内置的只读 `review` agent：它能读文件、搜索、查 LSP、跑只读的 git 和 forge 命令，不能编辑文件、起子任务或跑会改文件的命令。命令默认在后台运行，结束后把结论交回主会话，由主会话转述。 `task` 的前台/后台由提示词里的准则判断，代码不做启发式分类。默认走前台；需要用户输入或确认、会影响与主会话共享的状态、结果是下一步的直接输入、或是主会话能直接回答的快速查询时，一律走前台。同时满足以下几点才走后台：你表示会同时做别的事（“同时”“不用等”这类说法）或明确要求后台；委派的工作只读，或只写你和主会话都不会碰的文件；结果一条消息能说完。此时主会话先委派、不预先调查，再继续你同时要求的前台工作；没有剩余才简短回复并结束回合，结果稍后以一条消息送回。agent 或命令可以声明执行方式（`execution`），声明优先于提示词准则；交互型 agent 恒前台。理由和评测结果见 [ADR 0003](./docs/adr/0003-task-execution-classification.md)。 ### 思考塑形 🧪 实验性功能，默认关闭。思考型模型会把之前的思考内容在后续请求里回传，里面常有复述、被推翻的猜测和纠错过程。这个功能在后台把已完成的思考整理得更短，在后续步骤的请求里换用整理后的版本。整理失败、超时或没有可用的小模型时保留原文；原文一直存着，关掉功能后回放的就是原文。带签名或加密的思考不会碰。 我们想知道的是，开源模型的思考内容经过塑形之后，输出能力会不会提高。效果还在验证，所以标成实验性、默认关闭。整理用配置的 `small_model`，没配就用服务商自带的小模型： ```jsonc // graphagent.json { "small_model": "provider/small-model", // 建议选有 `none` 推理档位的模型 "reasoningDistillation": { "enabled": true, // 显式开启；默认 false }, } ``` ### 项目记忆 `/memory on` 开启后，GraphAgent 按项目保存偏好、决策和术语，只保存经你确认的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用一份。它不是代码索引，也不会压过你当前的输入和更高优先级的指令。 ### Goal 与 Loop `/goal <目标>` 让智能体在当前会话里跨回合自己推进一个目标，`/subgoal` 管子目标。每个回合结束后由外部 judge 判断进度：done 就收工，continue 就接着跑。总回合数有预算（默认 20），用尽后暂停，可以恢复。目标状态持久化，重启不丢。 ### 定时提醒 `/remind` 给当前会话设一个提醒。到点时，提醒会作为一条消息送进这个会话，由智能体转告你： ```text /remind 30m 看一下 CI 结果 /remind 2h 回复评审意见 /remind 09:00 站会前同步进度 /remind 明天 09:00 发周报 /remind every 1h 起身活动一下 /remind list /remind cancel rmd_1a2b3c4d ``` - `30m`、`2h`：从现在起的时长，单位只有 `m`（分钟）和 `h`（小时）。 - `09:00`：当天的这个钟点，已经过了就取明天；`明天 09:00`（也可以写 `tomorrow 09:00`）是明天的这个钟点。钟点按本机时区算。 - `every 1h`：重复提醒，首次在一个间隔之后，之后每隔一个间隔一次；间隔最短 5 分钟。 - `/remind list` 列出本会话待触发的提醒，`/remind cancel ` 取消一个。id 形如 `rmd_xxxxxxxx`，创建时的回执和 `list` 里都有。 提醒是持久化的，重启不丢，会话删除时一并删除。到点时如果会话空闲就送达，正忙就等当前回合结束后再送达；每次到期只送达一次。GraphAgent 关闭期间到期的提醒，下次在这个会话所在的目录启动时补发一次；重复提醒只补最近的一次，之后仍按原来的节奏。送达时比计划晚了一分钟以上，消息里会标明晚了多久。提醒文本原样放进这条消息，消息里要求智能体先告诉你，文本若是要做的事就接着做。 提醒只能由你用这条命令创建，模型没有创建提醒的工具；它只适用于主会话，在子会话里会被拒绝。 ### Hooks 兼容 Claude Code 的 hooks 协议。`hooks.json` 从全局配置目录和项目的 `.agents` 目录读取，执行类型有 command、HTTP、MCP 工具、prompt 和 agent 五种；项目里的 hooks 要先经过信任确认才会生效。`/import-claude` 把 `.claude/settings*.json` 审阅后转换进 `.agents/`，`/create-hook` 带你写新的 hook。详细说明见 [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)。 ### 上下文管理 一组管上下文的功能：限制工具输出的长度、限制每次输入的工具调用次数、自动压缩长会话。截断输出时会给出可执行的续读方式。 ## 其他改动 - `task` 可以用 `action: "resume"` 加 `task_id` 续接子智能体；后台子智能体完成时自动通知。 - 所有模型共用一份系统提示词，工具的用法写在各自的描述里，不按 Provider 挑提示词。 - 工具更严格，也更容易排错：`edit` 严格匹配（多处命中时列出候选行，找不到时给出最接近的片段），参数校验的报错带字段级提示。 - 支持用独立的 git worktree 管理工作目录。工作流不会自动隔离，并发的工作流要用不同的 worktree，或者串行跑。 - 会话创建时可指定 DAG 模式；TUI 页脚显示开关状态，状态接口返回可用性、并发与节点上限、token 预算用量。 - `config_assistant`（命令 `ocfg`）是一个用 Go 写的独立 TUI，用来定位、校验和编辑配置。 ## 快速开始 预构建的二进制（Linux、macOS，附 SHA256SUMS）在 [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) 页，解压后把 `graphagent` 放进 PATH，在项目目录里运行。v2.0 起不再发布 Windows 原生版本，也不再运行 Windows 集成测试；Windows 用户请安装 WSL，在 WSL 中按 Linux 方式安装使用。仓库里现有的 `oc` 安装脚本会在 v2.1 删除，安装和升级都并入主程序，见路线图。GraphAgent 不发布到 npm、brew 和 scoop，上游的 `opencode-ai` 装的是上游 opencode，不是 GraphAgent。 从源码运行需要 `package.json` 里 `packageManager` 固定的 Bun，以及 `.node-version` 指定的 Node： ```bash bun install bun dev <项目目录> # 启动 TUI；不带目录时在 packages/graphagent 里运行 ``` 启动之后，给它一件有阶段、有并行空间的活就行，不用先写任何 DAG 配置： ```text /dag-auto 把 auth 和 server 两个包迁移到新 API，最后跑集成测试 ``` 想把常用的图固定下来，就存成 `.agents/workflows/parallel-migrate.yaml`，之后说一句“跑 parallel-migrate 工作流”就按名字启动。下面这份 spec 里，两个迁移节点在同一波次并行，`assemble` 等它们都完成才开始： ```yaml title: 并行迁移 config: name: parallel-migrate nodes: - id: discover name: discover worker_type: explore depends_on: [] required: true prompt_template: { inline: "列出所有需要迁移到新 API 的包。" } - id: migrate-auth name: migrate-auth worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 auth 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: migrate-server name: migrate-server worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 server 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: assemble name: assemble worker_type: build depends_on: [migrate-auth, migrate-server] prompt_template: { inline: "跑集成测试，汇总结果。" } ``` 安装步骤、完整性校验和源码构建的细节见 [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)。 ## 设计思路 我们把图当成一份可执行、可持久化、可检查的契约，不是给人看的流程图，也不是事后给提示词链加的箭头。边必须真的传递产出：下游不读上游的东西，这条依赖就该删，独立的工作直接并行。模板只是参考拓扑，主智能体可以按任务增删分支，但每次剪枝要写明理由。预测、复审和裁决由不同的角色做，门禁不能剪。迭代只是有界的局部改图，不存在隐藏的环。最后，代码和测试说了算，状态靠事件记录恢复，代价高的地方留给人暂停、单步、取消和重规划。 第一个完整的 DAG 引擎提交是 2026-07-02；论文 [What makes prompts a graph](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27578) 到 2026-07-30 才把显式结构、提示词与拓扑分离、可执行语义和“图是一等制品”这些想法归纳出来，比引擎晚了四周。 ## 路线图 v2.0 的剩余工作也在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪： - DAG 模式的行为面：并发池、预算与质量机制、节点权限自动裁决。 - workflow 工具接口收敛、工作流级 worktree、事件驱动邮箱与持久对账。 - agent 契约与 composer：内置调研、架构设计、原型设计 agent，并在 DAG 内组合公共 agent。 - PR 监听改为事件源；`/remind` 持久提醒；后台任务显示与子 agent 只读界面。 - v2.0.0 发布：版本推导、Breaking 清单、中英迁移指南与 Linux、macOS 冒烟。 - v2.1：安装与升级并入主程序，直接从 GitHub 检索新版本并升级，不再需要 `oc` 脚本；release 打包随之调整，macOS 上安装不用再输密码；配置也可以从 GitHub 仓库读取（[#1281](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues/1281)）。 这些都是计划，实际状态以里程碑为准。 ## 起源与许可 GraphAgent 起源于早期的 opencode（MIT，[anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode)），从 v2.0 起作为独立项目维护。 许可分两条：继承自上游的代码保持 MIT，包括被我们改过的上游文件，文本见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)；GraphAgent 新写的代码是 Apache-2.0，文本见 [LICENSE-APACHE](./LICENSE-APACHE)。精确的文件边界在 [LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt](./LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt)，[NOTICE](./NOTICE) 有摘要。再分发时请保留 NOTICE 里的版权与归属声明。 ## 文档 除 architecture.md 和功能清单外，下面的文档目前只有英文。 - [docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md)：v1 架构，包括组件与目录、客户端与协议、源码索引 - [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)：DAG 工作流的用法、配置和引擎细节 - [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)：安装、完整性校验和源码构建 - [docs/compaction-retry.md](./docs/compaction-retry.md)：Provider 重试与压缩请求 - [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)：事件、配置和验证方法 - [docs/功能清单.md](./docs/功能清单.md)：功能与源码入口索引 - [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)：开发指南 - [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)：贡献说明 ## 链接 [GitHub](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent) · [Issues](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues) · [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) · [里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7) · [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)

items.name: nika
items.description: Intent as Code: say what you want done, keep it as a file. Checked before it runs, run with the model you choose, proven afterwards. Rust engine, CLI/TUI and TypeScript SDK. AGPL-3.0 🦋
items.readme_text:
Say it once.
Keep it as a file.

Checked before it runs. Run with the model you choose. Proven afterwards.
Nika turns the AI work you repeat into a readable workflow that stays yours. Fully open source.

“Read ./data/orders.csv, keep only the rows whose status is paid, and write them to ./out/paid.csv.”
One sentence becomes a checked file; yes saves it, run it keeps the two paid rows, and /proof shows what the run recorded. The real Session of nika 0.123.0, restyled; no AI model is involved.

## What is Nika? Nika turns repeatable AI work into a small file you keep. Say what you want done, like *"every Monday, pull the action items out of my meeting notes"*, and Nika writes it as a readable `.nika` workflow. Before anything runs, its check shows what the workflow will do, which models and tools it uses, what it is allowed to touch and what it can cost, without calling a model. A workflow that could read your private data, take in untrusted content and send data out is refused until it asks a person first. You run it when you decide, with the model you choose, on your machine or through a provider's API, and every run leaves a tamper-evident record you can verify. One Rust binary with a terminal Session and a command line, plus a TypeScript SDK for your applications; local-first and fully open source (AGPL-3.0). | 1 · Say it | 2 · Check it | 3 · Run it | 4 · Prove it | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Describe the job; Nika writes a `.nika` file (or `nika compile` from a skeleton) | `nika check` audits it before any model is called | `nika run` with the model you choose | `nika trace verify` checks the run's record |

See it · Control · Trifecta · Try it · Examples · Why a file · Where it works · Limits · Docs

## See it in four steps ### 1 · Say it Describe the job in plain words. Nika writes it as a `.nika` file, shows you what it will do and what it can touch, and saves it only when you say `yes`. Nothing runs until you ask. The clip at the top is that Session; this is its first answer, as the plain view prints it: ```text nika › Read ./data/orders.csv, keep only the rows whose status is paid, and write them to ./out/paid.csv. ✓ recorded 3 requirements Nika proposes `compiled-workflow.nika`: Does 1. read_source · reads a file … 8. write_output · writes a file Runs when you ask (« run it ») · no schedule was asked Can touch external effects · none human approval at run · none Changes + `compiled-workflow.nika` · 97 lines · new Needs nothing more from you Nothing has run yet · `yes` saves these exact bytes and checks them · running is its own line (« run it ») ``` ### 2 · Check it Before anything runs, `nika check` reads the file and reports what it will do, what it may touch and what it can cost. It calls no model and spends nothing.

Two mistakes caught before anything runs, the fix, and the clean re-check. Every line is captured from the real CLI.

### 3 · Run it You run it when you decide, with the model you choose. Here a local model, through Ollama, writes a meeting's action items as typed JSON.

The audit first, then a real run on a local model (ollama/llama3.2:3b); the clip names the release each part was captured with. Nothing leaves the machine.

### 4 · Prove it Every run leaves a hash-chained record. `nika trace verify` reads it back, and when a single byte changes it names the line where the chain breaks. Runs are also signed once this machine has a run-signing key. Mint it once with `NIKA_KEYCHAIN=off nika key init`: the key lands in `~/.nika/keys/` (mode `0600`), where terminal runs, scripts, CI, the TypeScript SDK and `nika serve` all read it, and later runs report `SEALED` in `nika trace verify` and `/proof`. Without the variable, a terminal on a Linux desktop can keep the key in the Secret Service, which only terminal runs open (`nika key align` copies it to the files), and on a Mac whose keychain holds a key from Nika 0.122 or older, `nika key init` refuses: 0.123.0 and later never open the macOS keychain.

The chain read back intact, then one changed byte refused at the next line. A mock/echo rehearsal captured from the real CLI; the scan is an illustration.

## You stay in control ### It refuses the lethal trifecta before a token is spent A workflow that can read your private data, take in content nobody vetted (a web page, a tool's answer, a command's output) and send data out is one injected instruction away from a leak. Simon Willison named this the [lethal trifecta](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/). `nika check` reads it from the permits, then follows the untrusted content from step to step, through a model's answer and into child workflows. When all three meet, it refuses the file until a person must say yes first. This workflow reads a note, fetches a public page, asks a local model for a digest and posts it to Slack: ```yaml nika: page-digest model: ollama/llama3.2:3b permits: fs: { read: ["./notes/today.md"] } net: { http: ["news.ycombinator.com", "hooks.slack.com"] } tools: ["nika:fetch", "nika:read", "nika:notify"] tasks: page: invoke: tool: "nika:fetch" args: { url: "https://news.ycombinator.com/" } notes: invoke: tool: "nika:read" args: { path: "./notes/today.md" } digest: with: { page: "${{ tasks.page.output }}", notes: "${{ tasks.notes.output }}" } infer: prompt: "Pick the three stories that matter for my notes.\nNotes: ${{ with.notes }}\nPage: ${{ with.page }}" max_tokens: 400 post: with: { digest: "${{ tasks.digest.output }}" } invoke: tool: "nika:notify" args: { target: "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX", message: "${{ with.digest }}" } ``` The page never reaches Slack directly, only through the model's digest. The check follows it anyway and refuses the file with exit code 2: ```text nika check · page-digest.nika ✔ PLAN 3 waves · 4 tasks · max parallelism 2 … ✖ TRIFECTA [NIKA-SEC-009] lethal trifecta complete · human gate required — untrusted content from `page` reaches egress task `post` while private read + untrusted ingress + external egress are all permitted … ``` Drop any one of the three and there is nothing to refuse. To keep all three, put a question in front of them: a `nika:prompt` with no default, whose answer the fetch, the read and the post each require. ```yaml approve: invoke: tool: "nika:prompt" args: { message: "Read my notes, fetch Hacker News and post a digest to Slack?" } page: with: { go: "${{ tasks.approve.output }}" } when: ${{ with.go == true }} invoke: tool: "nika:fetch" args: { url: "https://news.ycombinator.com/" } ``` With `nika:prompt` added to `permits.tools`, and the same `go` binding and `when:` line on `notes` and `post`, the check passes with exit code 0: ```text ✔ TRIFECTA no lethal trifecta over the declared permits: without a human gate layers · valid ✔ · access ready ✔ · capacity fit ✔ · run ready ✔ ``` A gate that only looks like one is refused too: a prompt with a `default:` answers itself and guards nothing (`NIKA-SEC-009` stays), and a step that still runs after a "no" fails `NIKA-SEC-014`. At a terminal the run asks; in CI it pauses with exit 4, as [shown below](#it-asks-before-it-acts). Every verdict here was captured from nika 0.124.0. [NIKA-SEC-009](https://nika.sh/language/errors/NIKA-SEC-009) explains the rule; Meta's [Agents Rule of Two](https://ai.meta.com/blog/practical-ai-agent-security/) states the same principle for agents. ### It tells you the cost before the first token `nika check` prices a workflow from its model's catalog price and the output limit each step declares. Set a budget below that ceiling and the run refuses to start: no model is called and nothing is spent.

Unbounded until one line declares max_tokens, then a hard ceiling of $0.0614; a $0.05 budget refuses the run (exit 2). Prices are catalog estimates, not invoices; no model was called.

### It asks before it acts A step can wait for a person. At your terminal it asks; in CI, where nobody can answer, the run pauses safely with exit 4 and prints the one line that resumes it.

Nothing ships without a yes: asked at a terminal, paused in CI, resumed by the printed line with the finished build reused. Every terminal line is captured from the real CLI; the door is an illustration.

## Try it in two minutes ### 1 · Install ```sh curl -LsSf https://nika.sh/install.sh | sh ```
Homebrew, npm, a container, a release archive, Nix or Windows - **Homebrew:** `brew install nika-open/tap/nika` - **npm**, the binary plus the TypeScript SDK: `npm install @nika-open/nika` (the `nika` command lands in `node_modules/.bin`). The package bundles the engine of its own version: check `nika --version`. - **A container** (Linux, amd64 and arm64), built from the same release binaries: `docker run --rm ghcr.io/supernovae-st/nika:0.124.4 --version`. Mount a project to check or run its files, for example `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ghcr.io/supernovae-st/nika:0.124.4 check hello.nika`. Images up to 0.124.4 are at `ghcr.io/supernovae-st/nika`; later releases publish theirs at `ghcr.io/nika-open/nika`. - **A release archive:** download one from the [latest release](https://github.com/nika-open/nika/releases/latest). Every release ships a checksum manifest, a GitHub attestation and SLSA provenance; [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md#what-a-user-can-prove) gives the three verification commands. Releases up to 0.124.4 were built in `supernovae-st/nika`, and that organization serves their attestations: `gh attestation verify nika-macos-arm64-0.124.4.tar.gz --owner supernovae-st --signer-repo supernovae-st/nika`. Later releases verify with `--repo nika-open/nika`. - **Nix:** `nix profile install github:nika-open/nika/v0.124.4` builds the release from the repository's flake. Without the tag, the flake builds the default branch, which can be ahead of the latest release. - **Windows:** use WSL2 and the Linux binary. Native Windows binaries are not shipped.
### 2 · Say what you want This first job needs no AI account: Nika's deterministic compiler settles it without calling a model. Make a folder with a small spreadsheet and open the Session: ```sh mkdir -p orders-demo/data && cd orders-demo cat > data/orders.csv <<'EOF' order_id,customer,status,amount 1001,Juniper Books,paid,18.00 1002,Kestrel Cafe,pending,9.50 1003,Linden Studio,paid,13.50 1004,Moss Supply,refunded,6.00 EOF nika ``` At the prompt, type: ```text Read ./data/orders.csv, keep only the rows whose status is paid, and write them to ./out/paid.csv. ``` Nika proposes a `.nika` file and shows what it will do, what it can touch and the result of its check. **Nothing has run yet.** Type `yes` to save the file, then `run it`. `out/paid.csv` gets the header and the two paid rows, and `/proof` shows what the run's record proves, and what it does not. > [!TIP] > Nika works only inside the folder you start it in. `/show` prints the > proposal's exact bytes, `/meaning` maps your request clause by clause, > and `no` discards it. `Ctrl+T` switches the view to full screen and back, > and `nika --plain` gives the same Session as plain lines. The > [Session guide](docs/usage/conversational-session.md) covers questions, > changes, spending ceilings and `/restore`. > > In a Git repository, the Session leaves `.gitignore` alone: before you > commit, add `.nika/traces/` (run records can hold file contents and model > outputs) and the Session's own `.nika/*.ndjson` and > `.nika/session-state.json`. After a run, the Session reminds you when > traces are not ignored. ### 3 · Add a model Most open-ended requests need a model to write the workflow, and workflows such as summaries call a model each time they run. Nika reads provider keys from your environment, so keep yours in your shell startup file. For DeepSeek: ```sh # in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc, then open a new terminal export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY='your-key' ``` The first request that needs a model shows a numbered choice: answer `2 deepseek/deepseek-flash`. Nika keeps the choice for later Sessions, and `/intelligence` changes it. Other API providers and local engines (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM) work too: `nika catalog` lists them. Your provider meters and bills these calls; Nika's cost figures are catalog estimates, not invoices. ### 4 · Use the file directly A workflow is an ordinary file. The command line compiles, checks, runs and verifies it. This offline lesson needs no provider: ```sh nika compile hello hello.nika nika check hello.nika nika run hello.nika nika trace verify ``` ▶ [Watch these four commands run](media/gifs/full-loop.optimized.gif), exactly as captured from the CLI. `hello` always uses `mock/echo`, a stand-in model that echoes the prompt, even when provider keys are present. It proves that the workflow runs, not that a model answered. Each run records its trace under `.nika/traces/`, and creating the file adds that directory to `.gitignore`. `nika trace verify` checks the latest trace's integrity, not the truth of an AI answer. ## What you can hand to Nika | You say | Nika keeps | Watch | |---|---|---| | *"Read `./data/orders.csv`, keep only the rows whose status is paid, and write them to `./out/paid.csv`."* | A workflow that reads one file and writes one file. No AI model is involved. | [▶ The Session](media/gifs/first-session.optimized.gif) | | *"Pull the action items out of my meeting notes."* | A workflow that asks a local model and writes the items as typed JSON. | [▶ A local run](media/gifs/nika-hero.optimized.gif) | | *"Every Friday, turn `CHANGELOG.md` into release notes."* | A workflow your coding agent writes with the Nika plugin; the check catches its mistake before anything runs. | [▶ With your agent](media/gifs/agent-plugin.optimized.gif) | | *"Rate the risk of each pull request."* | A workflow the Nika GitHub Action checks whenever a pull request changes it: one comment carries the verdict. | [▶ In your pull requests](media/gifs/pr-check-comment.optimized.gif) | ## Why a file, and not a chat? A chat answer is gone when the conversation ends, and the next one can differ. A `.nika` file stays: you read it, check it, run it again and review its changes like any other file in your project. - **Say it once.** The request you would retype in a chat every week is kept as a file that runs again. ▶ [Watch a weekly request become a file](media/gifs/chat-to-workflow.optimized.gif) - **Read it before it runs.** Every workflow has the same shape: nine sections and four kinds of step, in a file you can open and review. ▶ [Watch one taken apart](media/gifs/spec-anatomy.optimized.gif) - **It touches only what it declares.** The file lists what it may read, write and reach. The check refuses the step that reaches past it. ▶ [Watch the check catch an escape](media/gifs/permits-audit.optimized.gif) - **Failures are planned for.** A step can name its fallback: the run finishes, the output says it is stale, and the record keeps the failure. ▶ [Watch a missing feed absorbed](media/gifs/on-error-recover.optimized.gif) - **Parallel where it can be.** Steps that do not depend on each other run side by side, in waves the check plans before the run. ▶ [Watch a workflow run in waves](media/gifs/dag-execution.optimized.gif) Every clip on this page shows real files and terminal lines captured from the binary, names the release it was captured with, and says what it illustrates. The [media index](media/README.md#feature-clips) lists them all and how they are made. ## Works where you already work Nika comes to the tools you already use. Your coding agent can write the file for you, and the check keeps it honest:

Your agent writes it, Nika checks it, you keep it. The agent session is an illustration; the checks and the rehearsal run are captured from the real CLI.

| Where | What you get | Watch | |---|---|---| | **Your coding agent** · [nika-plugins](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-plugins) | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others learn to write a workflow, check it and repair what the check finds. | ▶ [above](media/gifs/agent-plugin.optimized.gif) | | **Your editor** · `nika lsp` | The language server inside the binary: the check's findings as you type, in any LSP client. The VS Code extension ([nika-vscode](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-vscode)) stays at 0.120 and is not qualified with 0.124; point its `nika.server.path` at your 0.124 binary ([known limits](https://docs.nika.sh/changelog/known-limits#the-vs-code-extension-stays-at-0-120)). | ▶ [The audit, as you type](media/gifs/editor-diagnostics.optimized.gif) | | **Your pull requests** · [nika-action](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-action) | One comment with the verdict, before anyone spends a token. | ▶ [Every pull request gets a verdict](media/gifs/pr-check-comment.optimized.gif) | | **Your app** · [nika-client](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-client) | Run a workflow from TypeScript ([the package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nika-open/nika)), get a typed result and verify its receipt, with the engine the package bundles or against your `nika serve`. | ▶ [Run it from your app, prove what ran](media/gifs/typescript-client.optimized.gif) · ▶ [One client, two doors](media/gifs/sdk-doors.optimized.gif) | ### From your application `npm install @nika-open/nika` brings the TypeScript SDK and the engine of its own version (Node.js 22 or newer, on macOS or Linux with glibc). Run `NIKA_KEYCHAIN=off ./node_modules/.bin/nika key init` once, so the engine your app starts can seal each run's record. Then, beside a `hello.nika`, this is the package's quick start: ```ts import { Nika, isNikaRunSucceeded } from '@nika-open/nika'; const nika = new Nika({ cwd: process.cwd() }); // The engine checks the file first: a workflow it refuses throws here and never starts. const run = await nika.run<{ greeting: string }>('hello.nika', { maxCostUsd: 0 }); const result = await run.result(); // A failed run is data you read, not an exception. if (!isNikaRunSucceeded(result) || !result.receipt) { console.error(result.status, result.error?.code, result.error?.message); process.exit(1); } console.log(result.outputs?.greeting); // Ask the engine to verify the run's tamper-evident record. const proof = await nika.traceVerify(result.receipt); console.log(proof.verified ? 'receipt verified' : `not verified: ${proof.reason}`); ``` Save it as `demo.mts` (top-level `await` needs a module) and run `node demo.mts`: Node.js 22.18 or newer runs the TypeScript as is. The [SDK quick start](https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/start/quickstart) gives the `hello.nika` this program runs. To reach a `nika serve` instead of the bundled engine, keep the methods and change the options of two lines: ```ts const nika = new Nika({ url, token, allowInsecureHttp: true }); const run = await nika.run<{ greeting: string }>('hello.nika', { idempotencyKey }); ``` `url` and `token` name the server and its bearer token. Plain `http://` is accepted only to a loopback host, and only with `allowInsecureHttp: true`. Over HTTP, `run()` needs an `idempotencyKey` you own (a retry with the same key returns the same job) and refuses `maxCostUsd`: the server applies its own per-run ceiling, USD 1 by default. `hello.nika` is then a served name, the workflow's path from the server's project root. [nika-client](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-client) documents the whole API.

Your app asks, the engine decides, the receipt proves it. The code is the quick start above, which the capture ran, with lines 3 and 6 also shown as its server driver ran them against nika serve. Every event, verdict, hash and version on screen was captured from @supernovae-st/nika 0.124.0, the engine it bundles and nika serve in a mock/echo rehearsal; the cards, lanes, packets and pacing are illustration.

## Know the limits - **0.124 is the current release line.** Work stays focused on maintenance, security and the media capabilities workflows need; native video is planned for 0.125. The 0.123.x line is the previous one, and there is no hosted service. The known limits are listed in plain words, each with a way around it: [Known limits in 0.124](https://docs.nika.sh/changelog/known-limits). - **Some requests cannot be expressed.** Nika then says what stopped it and writes nothing. - **A clean check is not a true answer.** It describes a file's structure and boundary; it does not prove that model output is right. - **The trifecta check judges permits and flow, not words.** It does not read a page or a model's answer for injected instructions, and a person who answers yes approves what follows. On a harness seat, what `permits:` covers is listed per seat ([harness agents](docs/usage/harness-agents.md)). - **This README describes the released 0.124.4.** Compare `nika --version` with the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), which lists what each release changed. Until the next release, each change merged after 0.124.4 is described in its own file under [`changelog.d/`](changelog.d/README.md), and the release folds those files into the changelog.
The four building blocks | Verb | What it does | |---|---| | `infer` | Ask a model to produce an answer | | `invoke` | Call a native tool, MCP tool or another workflow | | `exec` | Run a command | | `agent` | Let a model use allowed tools for a bounded number of turns | A workflow uses only the verbs its job needs. The orders workflow at the top uses `invoke` alone: eight steps over five builtin tools (`nika:read`, `nika:convert`, `nika:jq`, `nika:assert` and `nika:write`), with no model and no shell.
Compile from the command line `nika compile --list` lists exact skeletons. Preview one with `nika compile --json`, then answer its stable questions with repeatable `--answer KEY=JSON_LITERAL`. An incomplete result includes its candidate and questions; it does not write a file. Only a Ready candidate plus an explicit destination writes. Existing destinations require `--force`. For an accepted source, a conservative constant edit uses the same core: ```sh nika compile --base workflow.nika --change 'Set const.topic to "new topic"' --json ``` Add `--output edited.nika` to materialize a Ready edit. The base source remains explicit. Unresolved intent stays incomplete without a substitute workflow. `--authoring-model` seats a model to interpret free intent and revise text. No request count is imposed by default: creation ends on a result, a failure, no progress or a cancellation. `--authoring-max-calls N` sets an explicit ceiling (an ACP harness counts its invocations; its own requests are unknown), and typed repairs or samples that cannot fit under it are refused before any request. `--authoring-strategy` selects `escalate`, `only`, `sketch` or `off`. The compiler checks the proposed source and its fidelity to the request. This is not a guarantee of arbitrary-language understanding, and Graph editing is not implemented by this CLI. Compile's Check preview judges source only. `nika check` and `nika run` judge the actual environment separately. For a real model, choose the provider and access explicitly; the [model setup documentation](https://docs.nika.sh) explains local, API and supported harness choices. On a harness seat an `agent:` task runs the application's own tools: [what `permits:` covers there](docs/usage/harness-agents.md), and what it does not, is listed per seat and printed by `nika check`.
Before sharing a workflow or a run Share the workflow, not credentials or private data. Review file paths and tool access. Keep secrets out of source control. Run journals can contain the data and outputs the workflow processed. The `.nika/traces/` directory is a data-at-rest surface: it inherits the sensitivity of everything the run read. Exclude it from Git unless you deliberately intend to publish those records, and treat them with the same care as their source data. After a run, `nika trace verify` verifies the latest journal. Compare its head with the one printed by the run. This checks the record, not the AI's judgement.
## 🦋 The Nika family | | Repository | What it gives you | |---|---|---| | 🦋 | **[nika](https://github.com/nika-open/nika)** | **The engine and CLI: write, check, run and verify AI workflows** | | 📖 | [nika-docs](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-docs) | The documentation, live at [docs.nika.sh](https://docs.nika.sh) | | 📜 | [nika-spec](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-spec) | The language specification and the suite that proves an engine follows it | | 🧩 | [nika-vscode](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-vscode) | The editor extension, frozen at 0.120 and not qualified with 0.124: use `nika lsp` and the JSON Schema | | 🟦 | [nika-client](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-client) | Run and verify workflows from TypeScript | | ✅ | [nika-action](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-action) | A GitHub Action that posts a `nika check` verdict on your pull requests | | 🚀 | [nika-actions-starter](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-actions-starter) | A ready template: workflows, editor setup and CI from the first push | | 📦 | [nika-registry](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-registry) | Shareable workflows, pinned and re-verified | | 🤖 | [nika-plugins](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-plugins) | Teaches your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…) to write Nika | | 🍺 | [homebrew-tap](https://github.com/nika-open/homebrew-tap) | `brew install nika-open/tap/nika` | | 🐙 | [gh-nika](https://github.com/nika-open/gh-nika) | The Nika CLI as a GitHub CLI extension | | 🏛️ | [nika-estate](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-estate) | Where each file in Nika's core repositories comes from, declared and re-checkable | This repository is the one executable: it parses, checks, runs and traces every workflow. The language is defined by the specification, and the other repositories drive this engine without adding to its authority. ## Go further [Session guide](docs/usage/conversational-session.md) · [Examples](examples/README.md) · [Documentation](https://docs.nika.sh) · [TypeScript SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nika-open/nika) · [Editor extension (0.120, not qualified with 0.124)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=supernovae.nika) · [Open specification](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-spec) · [Registry](https://github.com/nika-open/nika-registry) · [Planning archive](https://github.com/orgs/supernovae-st/projects/3) · [Website](https://nika.sh) Nika 0.124 is the current open-source release line, usable today and maintained. The engine is [AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE); the specification and the TypeScript SDK are Apache-2.0. Created and maintained by Thibaut Mélen ([@ThibautMelen](https://github.com/ThibautMelen)) · SuperNovae Studio.

items.name: bike4mind
items.description: The open-core AI workbench — notebooks, agents, RAG, voice, and images across any model: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, or local via Ollama/vLLM. BSL 1.1, auto-converting to Apache-2.0 on a two-year clock. Your AI keeps running when theirs doesn't.
items.readme_text:
# Bike4Mind **Your bicycle for the mind in the age of AI.** An open-core AI knowledge platform — a multi-model workspace where notebooks, autonomous agents, and a RAG knowledge engine work together to augment any cognitive task. [![Chat on Bike4Mind](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Bike4Mind-6d28d9)](https://app.bike4mind.com) [![License: BUSL-1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BUSL--1.1-blue)](./LICENSE) [![Discussions](https://img.shields.io/badge/community-Discussions-24292f)](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind/discussions) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bike4mind/bike4mind?style=flat&label=stars&color=6d28d9)](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind)
--- ## What is Bike4Mind? Bike4Mind is an AI-powered knowledge platform that wires a superset of AI technologies together behind one workspace. Bring your own models, keep your data, and let agents do the heavy lifting. - **Notebooks** — the core workspace: chat, documents, and context in one place, across any model. - **Multi-LLM by design** — swap freely between **Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, Ollama** (local), and more, plus image models (GPT-Image-2, Nano Banana, FLUX). - **Quest Master** — autonomous, multi-step task planning: text and image generation, vision review, web search, math, code, and human-in-the-loop steps, run in parallel. - **AI Agents** — autonomous ReAct-style agents that carry out complex tasks against your tools and knowledge. - **Knowledge Engine** — RAG over your documents: smart chunking, vector search, collections, and tagging so agents can reason about what you know. - **Artifacts** — reusable snippets, documents, and visualizations produced by agents, with a built-in publish-and-share layer. Try the hosted service at **[app.bike4mind.com](https://app.bike4mind.com)**, or self-host the open core on your own infrastructure (below). ## Open core Bike4Mind is **open core**. The engine is public and self-hostable; the multi-tenant hosted service is our business. - **Open** (this repo, BUSL-1.1): the agent engine, LLM adapters, CLI, data models, and the self-host path — published as `@bike4mind/*` packages. - **Commercial / closed**: operating the multi-tenant hosted service — billing, entitlements, hosted infrastructure — and premium overlays such as Overwatch. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#the-openclosed-boundary) for the exact open/closed boundary. ## Quickstart **Hosted (fastest):** sign in at **[app.bike4mind.com](https://app.bike4mind.com)** — nothing to install. **Self-host:** run the open core on your own hardware with Docker — no AWS account or cloud provider required. See the **[Self-Host Quickstart](./SELF_HOST.md)**. In short: ```bash # 1. Copy the env template, then generate JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET / # SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY (see SELF_HOST.md) and add your model keys cp .env.selfhost.example .env.selfhost # 2. Bring up the stack (app + MongoDB + object storage + queues + mail catcher) docker compose -f compose.selfhost.yaml --env-file .env.selfhost up -d ``` Bike4Mind then runs at `http://localhost:3000`; sign-in code emails land in the bundled Mailpit at `http://localhost:8025`. The self-host image is published to `ghcr.io/bike4mind/bike4mind-selfhost`. ## Develop Bike4Mind is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (Node 24). ```bash pnpm i -r # install pnpm turbo:core:build # build the @bike4mind/* core packages pnpm turbo:typecheck:fast # type check pnpm turbo:test # run tests ``` Project layout: `apps/client` (Next.js SPA + pages API backend), `packages/cli` (interactive CLI + ReAct agent), `b4m-core/*` (the `@bike4mind/*` engine packages), `packages/database` (Mongoose models + migrations). Realtime WebSocket fanout ships as a separate `@bike4mind/subscriber-fanout` image. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full guide. Building an app that signs users in with Bike4Mind and bills AI usage to their accounts? See [Building an app on Bike4Mind](docs-site/docs/developers/building-on-b4m.md). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome — fork → topic branch → PR → squash-merge. All contributors sign a lightweight CLA on their first PR (you keep your copyright). Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and our [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Questions and self-hosting help go in [Discussions](https://github.com/bike4mind/bike4mind/discussions). ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately — see [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). Do not open public issues for security problems. ## License Bike4Mind is licensed under the **[Business Source License 1.1](./LICENSE)** with a broad Additional Use Grant: - ✅ You **may** read, modify, redistribute, and make production use of the code — including self-hosting it for your organization's own internal use, and building or commercializing your own products on top of it. - ❌ You **may not** offer the software to third parties as a competing hosted/managed service (a "Bike4Mind Service", as defined in the LICENSE). - 🕓 Each released version **converts to Apache-2.0** two years after its public release. This license will never be tightened. For alternative licensing, contact **licensing@bike4mind.com**. © 2026 Bike4Mind, Inc.

items.name: slax-reader
items.description: Open-source, AI-powered read-it-later — save web pages, highlight, and discuss
items.readme_text: # Slax Reader Open-source, AI-powered read-it-later — save web pages, highlight, and discuss. ![Slax Reader web app](docs/assets/web-inbox.jpeg) ## Get Slax Reader - **Website**: [slax.com/reader](https://slax.com/reader/) - **Web**: [r.slax.com](https://r.slax.com/) - **iOS**: [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/slax-reader-ai-read-later/id6596730998) - **Android**: [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.slax.reader) - **Chrome Extension**: [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/slax-reader/gdnhaajlomjkhahnmiijphnodkcfikfd) (works on Edge too) Follow [@SlaxReader](https://x.com/SlaxReader) on X for updates. ## What it does - **Permanent snapshots** — saved pages stay readable even after the original link dies. - **AI reading aids** — outlines, summaries, and in-context answers while you read. - **Highlight and discuss** — annotate any passage, then share the page; anyone with the link can join the discussion. ## Repository structure This monorepo hosts all Slax Reader code: | Path | Description | | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `apps/web` | Web frontend ([r.slax.com](https://r.slax.com/)) | | `apps/extension` | Browser extension (Chrome/Edge) | | `apps/mobile` | Expo / React Native Android and iOS app | | `apps/api` | API server (Cloudflare Workers: Core, Edge, AI and Browser) | | `apps/cli` | Command-line client | | `packages/contracts` | Shared API, domain and event contracts (`@slax-reader/contracts`) | | `packages/frontend-types` | Shared Web/Extension implementation types | | `packages/frontend-utils` | Shared frontend utilities | | `packages/reader-embed` | Portable reader assets and PDF runtime for mobile hosts | | `packages/selection` | Shared highlighting and annotation engine | | `deploy/` | Public API template and local app infrastructure | | `docs/` | Web, Extension, API, CLI and mobile development docs | | `tests/e2e` | End-to-end tests | | `tooling/` | Command dispatchers and repository tooling | Shared libraries belong in `packages` when at least two apps use them. See the [Web architecture](docs/web/architecture.md) for the current application and package boundaries. ## Development and self-hosting Install dependencies once from the repository root: ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` The root exposes one dispatcher per application while each app keeps its concrete command list: ```bash pnpm preflight pnpm setup:all pnpm api -- dev pnpm web -- dev pnpm extension -- dev ``` `pnpm preflight` checks the Node.js/pnpm runtime and the API, Web, and Extension module states without changing local files or services. After configuration is prepared, `pnpm setup:all` runs API setup, Web setup, and Extension setup in order. Run the three `dev` commands separately; setup never starts application servers. The API's `setup` command prepares local dependencies and exits; `dev` starts Workers separately. Use `pnpm api -- setup` when only the API needs to be initialized again. Remote deployment and migrations remain explicit operations with their safety checks. See the [API development guide](docs/api/DEVELOPMENT-DOCUMENT-EN.md) ([中文](docs/api/DEVELOPMENT-DOCUMENT-CN.md), [日本語](docs/api/DEVELOPMENT-DOCUMENT-JP.md)). Preflight distinguishes startup blockers (`当前无法启动`) from missing functionality (`可启动，但无法正常运行`), such as unavailable Docker or missing login settings. Both return exit code 1; optional features do not. See [Reading preflight results](docs/LOCAL-SETUP.md#reading-preflight-results) for status meanings and recovery steps. Web and Extension configuration lives alongside the API's under `deploy/local/`, distinguished by filename: `.env.web`/`.env.web.example` for Web, `.env.extension`/`.env.extension.example` for Extension. The API uses the public template [`deploy/cloudflare/api.toml.example`](deploy/cloudflare/api.toml.example) and ignored local configuration under `deploy/local/`. Secrets belong in ignored local environment files or platform secret stores; do not put them in tracked templates or browser bundles. API commands and API-specific configuration belong to [`apps/api/`](apps/api/), including Prisma configs under `prisma/` and deployment code under `script/deploy/`. The root `api` command forwards to the scripts declared by `apps/api/package.json`. Validation commands include: ```bash pnpm api -- gen:all pnpm api -- lint pnpm api -- typecheck pnpm api -- test pnpm api -- build ``` Shared HTTP types live in [`packages/contracts`](packages/contracts/README.md). Web, Extension, API and CLI code import the contract package and do not import application internals. ### CLI The [CLI](apps/cli/README.md) is published as `@slax-lab/reader-cli` with the `reader-cli` executable. It needs no local deployment configuration to build or test: ```bash pnpm cli -- typecheck pnpm cli -- build pnpm cli -- start --help pnpm cli -- test pnpm cli -- test:package pnpm test:cli-tooling ``` See [CLI development](docs/cli/DEVELOPMENT.md) and [automated npm/GitHub releases](docs/cli/RELEASE.md). Merges that change the CLI and increase its package version automatically create `cli-v<version>-dev` and `cli-v<version>-beta` GitHub Pre-Releases on `dev` and `beta`. Promotion to `main` creates `cli-v<version>` and publishes the same tested stable archive through npm OIDC and GitHub Release; no user-added Actions secret is required. ## Contributing Bug reports, features, and docs are all welcome. You can contribute without a development environment through [Web 开发与参与指南](docs/web/development.md) or [Extension development](docs/extension/development.md). Please follow our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Copyright is held by The Slax Reader Contributors — see [NOTICE](NOTICE) for details.

items.name: goethe
items.description: Serve your models fast on your own infra in 3 steps.
items.readme_text:
Run and share your models on your own infra in 3 steps, and run them fast.

If Goethe is useful to you, a ⭐ on GitHub helps others find it.

Goethe turns a Linux machine into your own API, compatible with OpenAI, Anthropic and LiteLLM clients. Install it, add a model, and point your apps, your team or your other machines at one address. Your prompts, your data and your models stay on hardware you control. ```bash curl -fsSL https://pkg.goethe.sh/install.sh | bash goethe ``` On Windows 10/11 (x64), elevated PowerShell (enables WSL2, then runs the same `install.sh` inside Ubuntu): ```powershell irm https://pkg.goethe.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` `goethe` on its own starts Goethe and, the first time, walks you through three steps: install a model, serve it through the API, and configure who can reach it. If you prefer plain commands, these do the same: ```bash # 1. Start Goethe and load a model goethe up goethe install nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 --load # 2. Share it goethe api expose vpn # or local, or public: this machine only, your VPN (recommended), or a public address goethe api keys create my-laptop # one key per app or person goethe api # the address to give your apps ``` On a 32 GB Blackwell GPU, `goethe models recommend` lists `meshapplied/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-NInfer` first. Anything that speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic or LiteLLM API can use it right away, all at the same address: the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, LiteLLM, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Open WebUI, coding assistants, or plain `curl`. ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="https://:8443/v1", api_key="goethe_sk_...") reply = client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], ) print(reply.choices[0].message.content) ``` ## Why Goethe - **Easy to serve.** Every model you load is served at the same URL; a request picks its model by name. - **Fast.** Use the custom kernel attachments to accelerate and optimise model capability. - **Private by default.** Nothing reaches the API until you allow it. Rate-limit, expire, scope or revoke keys at any time. - **Fits your network.** This machine only, a VPN, or a public IP. `goethe api expose` sets it. - **Many models, many GPUs.** Run several models side by side, split large models across GPUs, and keep other GPU software running next to Goethe. - **Always on.** Loaded models come back after a reboot or a crash. ## Where it runs | Environment | Examples | |---|---| | Your own hardware | Workstations and servers with one or more NVIDIA GPUs, including DGX Spark | | Cloud GPU virtual machines | AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle Cloud, Lambda, CoreWeave, Paperspace | | GPU containers | RunPod, Vast.ai, and Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit | Linux on x86_64 or ARM64 (glibc 2.30 or newer, for example Ubuntu 20.04+ or Debian 11+). Goethe recognises the cloud provider or container it runs in and shows the address to use from outside. ## GPU and CUDA compatibility | Architecture | Compute capability | GPUs | |---|---|---| | Blackwell | 12.0, 12.1 | GeForce RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DGX Spark (GB10) | | Blackwell data center | 10.0, 10.3 | B200, GB200, B300, GB300 | | Hopper | 9.0 | H100, H200, GH200 | | Ada | 8.9 | GeForce RTX 4090, RTX 6000 Ada, L40S, L40, L4 | | Ampere | 8.0, 8.6 | A100, A30, A40, A10, RTX A6000, GeForce RTX 3090 | Older GPUs (Volta, Turing) are not supported. A machine can mix GPU generations; each model runs on GPUs of one generation, and large models can be split across several GPUs. Goethe ships its own CUDA 13 runtime and compiler, so no CUDA toolkit is needed on the machine. What it needs is the NVIDIA driver: | NVIDIA driver | CUDA it offers | Goethe runs on | |---|---|---| | 580 or newer | 13.0 and newer | Every supported GPU | | 535 to 579 | 12.2 to 12.9 | Data-center GPUs (A100, H100, H200, B200, L40S, L4 and similar), through NVIDIA's CUDA forward compatibility | | Older than 535 | | Not supported; the installer offers to update the driver | GeForce and TITAN cards need driver 580 or newer. Enough GPU memory for the model is the only other requirement; `goethe models recommend` lists the models that fit. The llama.cpp build goethe downloads for GGUF models uses CUDA 12.8 libraries; NVIDIA lists the minimum driver of each CUDA release in its [CUDA compatibility table](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html). Drivers older than the 580 line above are unverified with goethe. Supported [model families and quantization formats](docs/user-guide.md#supported-models) are in the user guide. GGUF models (single GPU) and GGUF embedding models are served through llama.cpp. ## Known limits - Gated models need the license accepted on Hugging Face and a read token (install with `--hf-token`). This includes `orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-NVFP4`. - Optimised kernel packs (the 27B NVFP4 model, the ternary models and others) need `goethe login` on the node. A model that has only a pack and none for your GPU is refused before anything is downloaded. - If a model's kernel pack cannot run on your GPU, install or load stops with the reason. Add `--fallback` (or set `GOETHE_ALLOW_FALLBACK=1`) to serve it with the plain runtime instead. ## Documentation - **[User guide](docs/user-guide.md):** install, add models, share the API, and troubleshooting. - **[Command reference](docs/cli.md):** every `goethe` command and option. - **[Our models](docs/research-models.md):** the models we publish, and how fast they run. - **Full documentation:** [goethe.sh/docs](https://goethe.sh/docs). ## Repository layout | Path | What it is | |------|------------| | [`goethe/`](goethe/) | Goethe: the `goethe` command, the background service, the gateway and the installer | | [`lab/`](lab/) | `goethe-lab`: fit/registry helpers used in development and tests | | [`nvfp4-kernels/`](nvfp4-kernels/), [`ternary-kernels/`](ternary-kernels/) | GPU kernels behind our models | | [`docs/`](docs/) | User guide, command reference and model notes | Our models on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meshapplied) and at [goethe.sh/models](https://goethe.sh/models). ## License Goethe is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The license of each model you serve still applies. Goethe is built on third-party software, among them SGLang, PyTorch, FlashInfer, Triton, Hugging Face Transformers, nginx and NVIDIA's CUDA libraries. [NOTICE](NOTICE) lists them with their licenses.

items.description: 📊 Automated hourly benchmarks for 20+ NVIDIA NIM models — interactive dashboard, zero infra, self-hostable. Open-source & community-driven.
items.readme_text:
[![NIMStats Banner](https://capsule-render.vercel.app/api?type=waving&color=76b900&height=220§ion=header&text=NIMStats&fontSize=90&fontColor=ffffff&animation=fadeIn&fontAlignY=38&desc=Real-Time%20NVIDIA%20NIM%20Benchmark%20Dashboard&descSize=22&descAlignY=60&descAlign=50)](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/) [![CI](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/actions/workflows/benchmark.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/actions) [![Live Dashboard](https://img.shields.io/badge/🌐%20live-nimstats.maurodruwel.be-76b900?style=flat-square)](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/) [![Models](https://img.shields.io/badge/models-22-blue?style=flat-square)](https://build.nvidia.com/models) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-yellow?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/pulls) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/MauroDruwel/NIMStats?style=flat-square&color=gold)](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/stargazers)
> **Community-driven benchmarking of 22 NVIDIA NIM models — fully automated, zero infra cost, self-hostable in minutes.**
**[🚀 View Live Dashboard](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/) · [📖 Docs](#-quick-start) · [🤝 Contribute](#-contributing) · [💬 Discussions](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/discussions)**
--- ## ✨ What is NIMStats? NIMStats automatically benchmarks **22 NVIDIA NIM models** every hour using GitHub Actions and publishes the results to a beautiful, interactive dashboard. No servers, no subscriptions — just fork, add your API key, and go.
| 🏎️ Hourly Benchmarks | 📊 Interactive Charts | 🔁 Zero Infrastructure | 🌍 Fully Open-Source | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Automatic via GitHub Actions | Response time, throughput & trends | Static site + free CI/CD | Fork and self-host in minutes |
--- ## ⚡ Quick Start > Get your own benchmarking dashboard running in under 5 minutes. ### 1. Fork & Clone ```bash git clone https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats.git cd NIMStats ``` ### 2. Get a Free API Key Visit **[build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com)** → Create a free account → Copy your API key. ### 3. Add the Secret In your forked repo: **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret** | Name | Value | |------|-------| | `NIM_API_KEY` | Your NVIDIA NIM API key | ### 4. Deploy the Dashboard | Platform | Steps | |----------|-------| | **Cloudflare Pages** | Connect repo → auto-deploys on every push to `main` | | **GitHub Pages** | Settings → Pages → Deploy from `main` | | **Netlify / Vercel** | Connect repo for instant auto-deploy | ### 5. Run Your First Benchmark **Actions → Benchmark NVIDIA NIM Models → Run workflow** That's it — your dashboard auto-refreshes every hour. ✨ --- ## 📊 Dashboard Features
| Tab | What you get | |-----|-------------| | **📊 Overview** | 5 animated KPI cards · success trend charts · top-10 speed & throughput bars · model reliability pills | | **🏆 Leaderboard** | Composite score rankings · sortable columns · SVG sparklines · trend indicators (↑↓→) · provider chips | | **🔬 Explorer** | Per-model deep dive · response time history chart · error breakdown donut · availability heatmap | | **⏱ Timeline** | Filterable run history (All / 24h / 48h / 7d) · expandable run cards with full per-model detail | | **⚔️ Compare** | Head-to-head overlay chart · win-rate stats · side-by-side metric comparison | | **🔗 Public APIs** | Multiple category endpoints: `/top` (balanced), `/top/speed` (speed & tps), and `/top/intelligence` (capabilities) in both JSON and raw `.txt` formats. Perfect for integration with local scripts, scripts, or apps |
--- ## 🔌 Developer APIs NIMStats exposes lightweight, static API endpoints for querying the #1 model in different performance categories. Every time the hourly benchmark completes, these endpoints are updated. ### Available Endpoints | Category | Endpoint (JSON) | Endpoint (Plain Text) | Scoring Balance | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **⚖️ Balanced (Overall)** | [`/top`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top) | [`/top/model`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top/model) | **30%** Uptime + **30%** Intelligence + **20%** Avg Time + **20%** Throughput | | **🏎️ Speed & Throughput** | [`/top/speed`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top/speed) | [`/top/speed/model`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top/speed/model) | **50%** Avg Response Time + **50%** Throughput (TPS) | | **🧠 Model Intelligence** | [`/top/intelligence`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top/intelligence) | [`/top/intelligence/model`](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/top/intelligence/model) | **70%** Artificial Analysis Score + **30%** Uptime | ### JSON Response Schema ```json { "best_model": "nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning", "provider": "nvidia", "score": 71, "intelligence": 14.9, "uptime": 90.6, "avg_response_time_ms": 4736.7, "best_response_time_ms": 432.0, "avg_time_to_first_token_ms": 312.5, "avg_throughput_tps": 163.3, "total_runs": 720, "success_count": 652, "wins": 364, "last_seen": "2026-07-07T10:00:08Z", "generated_at": "2026-07-07T10:08:49Z" } ``` --- ## 🤖 Benchmarked Models
22 models across 11 providers — click to expand
| Provider | Model | Highlight | |----------|-------|-----------| | **DeepSeek** | `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` | Fast MoE, optimized for speed | | **DeepSeek** | `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro` | Professional-grade reasoning | | **Z-AI** | `z-ai/glm-5.2` | Superior code understanding | | **MiniMax** | `minimaxai/minimax-m2.7` | Efficient inference model | | **MiniMax** | `minimaxai/minimax-m3` | Latest MiniMax generation | | **NVIDIA** | `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` | NVIDIA's 120B flagship | | **NVIDIA** | `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` | Compact omni reasoning model | | **NVIDIA** | `nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5` | Nemotron Super 49B v1.5 | | **Moonshot** | `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` | Context-optimized model | | **OpenAI** | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | Open-source 120B | | **Google** | `google/gemma-4-31b-it` | Lightweight edge inference | | **Qwen** | `qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b` | Flagship Qwen (397B) | | **Qwen** | `qwen/qwen3.5-122b-a10b` | Mid-range Qwen 3.5 MoE | | **Qwen** | `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct` | Next-gen Qwen (80B MoE) | | **Mistral** | `mistralai/mistral-large-3-675b-instruct-2512` | Largest Mistral (675B) | | **Mistral** | `mistralai/mistral-medium-3.5-128b` | Efficient medium-scale Mistral | | **Mistral** | `mistralai/mistral-small-4-119b-2603` | Mistral Small 4 (119B) | | **Meta** | `meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct` | Llama 3.3 70B | | **Meta** | `meta/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct` | Llama 4 Maverick (128 experts) | | **Meta** | `meta/llama-3.2-90b-vision-instruct` | Multimodal 90B vision model | | **StepFun** | `stepfun-ai/step-3.5-flash` | Ultra-fast flash model | | **StepFun** | `stepfun-ai/step-3.7-flash` | Latest high-performance flash |
--- ## 🏗️ How It Works ```` ┌──────────────────── GitHub Actions (every hour) ──────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Job 1 — Group A │ │ Job 2 — Group B │ (parallel) │ │ │ N/2 NIM models │ │ N/2 NIM models │ │ │ └──────────┬──────────┘ └──────────┬──────────┘ │ │ └──────────────┬───────────────┘ │ │ ┌────────▼────────┐ │ │ │ Merge + commit │ → history.db committed to repo │ │ └─────────────────┘ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌──────────▼───────────┐ │ Cloudflare Pages │ → auto-deploys on push │ (static dashboard) │ index.html + history.db └──────────────────────┘ ```` **Parallel jobs = ~50% faster benchmarks** ⚡ --- ## 🛠️ Customization
Change the benchmark prompt Edit `PROMPT` in `scripts/test_models.py`: ```python PROMPT = "Your custom prompt here" ```
Add or remove models Use the model management script: ```bash # List models in DB vs test_models.py python scripts/manage_models.py list # Add a new model to ALL_MODELS python scripts/manage_models.py add your/custom-model # Remove a model from ALL_MODELS and purge its data from history.db python scripts/manage_models.py remove your/custom-model # Purge all DB models not in ALL_MODELS python scripts/manage_models.py purge ``` Or manually edit `ALL_MODELS` in `scripts/test_models.py`: ```python ALL_MODELS = [ "your/custom-model", # ... ] ```
Change the schedule Edit `.github/workflows/benchmark.yml`: ```yaml - cron: '0 */6 * * *' # Every 6 hours instead of every hour ```
Run locally ```bash # Serve the dashboard python3 -m http.server 8000 # Open http://localhost:8000 # Run benchmarks manually (requires NIM_API_KEY env var) export NIM_API_KEY=your_key_here python3 scripts/test_models.py ```
--- ## 📦 Data Storage `history.db` is a SQLite database persisted in the repo — the single source of truth. The browser loads it via [sql.js](https://sql.js.org/) (WebAssembly) and queries it entirely client-side. `scripts/results.json` is a temporary per-job artifact that is never committed. **Schema Architecture:** ```sql CREATE TABLE prompts ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, text TEXT UNIQUE ); CREATE TABLE models ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT UNIQUE, intelligence_score REAL DEFAULT NULL ); CREATE TABLE errors ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, text TEXT UNIQUE ); CREATE TABLE runs ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, timestamp TEXT NOT NULL, prompt_id INTEGER REFERENCES prompts(id), fastest_model_id INTEGER REFERENCES models(id), fastest_time INTEGER ); CREATE TABLE model_results ( run_id INTEGER REFERENCES runs(id), model_id INTEGER REFERENCES models(id), success INTEGER NOT NULL, error_id INTEGER REFERENCES errors(id), response_time INTEGER, tokens_generated INTEGER, total_tokens INTEGER, time_to_first_token INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, model_id) ); ``` **Benchmark parameters (default):** `temperature: 0.7` · `top_p: 0.9` · `max_tokens: 500` · OpenAI-compatible API. GLM-5.3 variants use `reasoning_effort: low` and `max_tokens: 2048` because thinking is always enabled. --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are what make the open-source community amazing. Any contribution you make is **greatly appreciated**! 1. **Fork** the repository 2. Create your feature branch: `git checkout -b feat/amazing-feature` 3. Commit your changes: `git commit -m 'feat: add amazing feature'` 4. Push to the branch: `git push origin feat/amazing-feature` 5. Open a **Pull Request** **Ideas for contributions:** - 🆕 Add new NIM models to the benchmark list - 📊 New chart types or dashboard widgets - 🌐 Internationalization / translations - 🐛 Bug fixes and performance improvements - 📖 Improve documentation Please read through open [Issues](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats/issues) before starting — someone might already be working on it! --- ## 🔗 Resources - [NVIDIA NIM API Documentation](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/) - [NVIDIA Model Catalog](https://build.nvidia.com/models) - [GitHub Actions Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) - [sql.js — SQLite in the browser](https://sql.js.org/) --- ## 📄 License Distributed under the **MIT License**. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) for details. ---
Made with ❤️ for the ML community · [⭐ Star this repo](https://github.com/MauroDruwel/NIMStats) if you find it useful! [![footer](https://capsule-render.vercel.app/api?type=waving&color=76b900&height=100§ion=footer)](https://nimstats.maurodruwel.be/)

items.name: Mingle
items.description: Bring your agent companion into the chat apps you already use. Runs on your machine, no server.
items.readme_text:
# Mingle English · [中文](README_CN.md) · [mingle.build](https://mingle.build) **Bring your agent companion into the chat apps you already use. Runs on your machine, no server.** Create an agent on your own computer: it has a name, a role, a memory and a home directory, and a coding agent you already use drives it. The agent joins your chat apps as a bot, where people can @-mention it, hand it tasks and hear back from it. - **One agent, every chat app, one memory.** The same agent is in your Feishu work group, your WeChat family chat and your Discord server at once, and remembers all of it. Ask it in WeChat what the team decided in Feishu this morning, or have it pass a message from Slack to Telegram. - **Your own chat apps.** No new chat platform. The agent shows up in the groups and direct messages you already have. - **The agent you already pay for.** It runs on the harness and subscription you have; Mingle adds no model and no bill. - **Several things at once.** Ask for something that takes a while and the agent works on it on the side, still answering everyone else, then replies under your message when it is done. - **Your data stays on your machine.** There is no Mingle server, no account and no telemetry. ## Works with | | | | --- | --- | | **Chat apps** | WeChat, WeCom, Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, Slack, Discord, Telegram; GitHub issues and pull requests, from an account of the agent's own; iMessage on a Mac, by texting yourself | | **Harnesses** | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build, Qwen Code, Qoder, CodeBuddy Code, DeepSeek Harness, Pi, Antigravity, Devin, Factory Droid, through [OAR](https://github.com/botiverse/oar) | | **Systems** | macOS, Windows, Linux | Mingle is in early development. The core works end to end with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Kimi Code. Feishu is verified on a real tenant; the other chat apps against their APIs and in tests. ## Install Download the desktop app for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/earayu/Mingle/releases/latest), or install it from a terminal: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/earayu/Mingle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh # macOS, Linux irm https://github.com/earayu/Mingle/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex # Windows (PowerShell) ``` The macOS app is signed and notarized by Apple. The Windows app is not signed yet: choose "More info → Run anyway". The app lives in the menu bar or tray, keeps Mingle running in the background, can open at login and updates itself. A harness you don't have yet can be installed and signed in from the app. ## Quick start In the app: **New agent**, give it a name and a role, pick a harness, then connect a chat app and follow the steps shown for it. Whoever scans the code, or sends the bot the 6-digit claim code the app shows, becomes the agent's owner. The same from source, with Node.js 24 and pnpm: ```sh git clone https://github.com/earayu/Mingle.git && cd Mingle pnpm install && pnpm build node dist/cli/main.js start # keep this running; opens the console in your browser node dist/cli/main.js agent create --name Alex --harness claude --role "You help me plan trips." echo "$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN" | node dist/cli/main.js connect alex telegram ``` Then send the bot a direct message from your own Telegram account; that makes you its owner. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR chat["Chat apps
WeChat · Feishu · Slack · Telegram · …"] <--> mingle["Mingle
on your computer"] mingle <--> harness["Your harness
Claude Code · Codex · …"] ``` - Mingle receives messages through each chat app's official bot API and hands them to the agent's single, long-lived harness session. iMessage, which has no bot API, runs locally on your own Apple ID. There is no cloud bridge. - The agent answers through the `mingle` command (reply, send, read and search chats, tasks, reminders, an address book); Mingle checks permissions and delivers. Owners can send `/stop`; there are no other session commands. - Each agent's home holds `ROLE.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `notes/`. Everything else lives in `~/.mingle` (`MINGLE_HOME`), including the log at `~/.mingle/logs/mingle.log` (`mingle log`). Bot credentials are kept only in the macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI or the Linux Secret Service. - The console and API listen on `127.0.0.1` only. ## For AI agents - **Using or explaining Mingle:** [mingle.build/llms.txt](https://mingle.build/llms.txt) summarizes the product and the CLI. Inside a session, `mingle manual` prints the agent's full guide. - **Working on this repository:** start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), the code map and working rules, then [docs/spec.md](docs/spec.md) for scope and architecture and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) before touching the interface. `pnpm check` (typecheck, lint, tests) must pass. ## Documentation - [Product design and architecture](docs/spec.md) (Chinese) - [Interface design](DESIGN.md) (Chinese) - [Remote SSH](docs/remote-ssh.md): run an agent on another machine (in development) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Releasing](docs/releasing.md) ## Feedback [Issues](https://github.com/earayu/Mingle/issues) are welcome, in English or Chinese. For a bug, include your version, system, harness, chat app and the relevant lines of `mingle log`. We aren't accepting pull requests for now. Report security problems [privately](https://github.com/earayu/Mingle/security/advisories/new) rather than in a public issue. For anything else, write to [earayu@gmail.com](mailto:earayu@gmail.com). ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
